LhzLaRmQppw.speaker: adnan
LhzLaRmQppw.speaker_note: Refers to himself by name ('this Adnan who keeps talking') and to leading prayer at his masjid in Syria.
LhzLaRmQppw.title: Ramadan Prep 2: The Beauty of Ramadan
LhzLaRmQppw.one_line: Five gifts (nafahat) Ramadan brings to the believer: repentance, fasting, the Quran, night prayer and sincerity, and how to receive each.
LhzLaRmQppw.summary: He opens by explaining why he teaches religion in Arabic: the language matters only because it is the language of the Quran and the Prophet, and that other community languages such as Urdu and Bengali deserve their own lessons. He then describes Ramadan as a nafha: a gift that comes to you whether or not you go to it. He lists five. Repentance: Ramadan overturns your routine, and such large disruptions are the best moment to drop a bad habit, but only if you name it precisely, while good habits are built by small steady increments. Fasting: the hardest act of worship, almost immune to showing off, which Allah claims as His own and rewards personally. The Quran: Ramadan's rank comes from the revelation, so the salaf set hadith aside to read; he asks for at least one reflective khatm. Night prayer: tarawih is named for rest, its sunnah is completing the Quran, people should stay with the imam until he finishes, may sit when tired, and must not neglect obligatory congregational prayers, especially Fajr. Sincerity: Ramadan clears distractions so the heart can turn to Allah, and the follower behind an imam has a rare freedom to enjoy the recitation. He ends by urging people to expose themselves to these gifts before they are taken away.

outline.heading: Opening
Trained in Arabic the hard way
outline.gist: He understands and loves explaining the deen only in Arabic. He spent years on grammar, morphology, rhetoric and oratory, took slaps from his teachers for every grammatical slip, and had to learn prosody and compose poetry on his feet before receiving his ijazah.

outline.heading: Why he will not translate
outline.gist: Translating mid-thought is the ugliest thing for a speaker: you reach a point in your chain of ideas and must go back and redo it in another language, like reformatting a device. He would rather give one khutbah in Arabic and another in English.

outline.heading: Arabic's worth is the Quran's worth
outline.gist: Every community should have lessons in the languages its people speak as well as in the language of the Book. Arabic's value is not Arabness: a language is worth as much as those who spoke it, and Allah and His Messenger spoke it. Urdu and Bengali speakers deserve lessons in their languages too.

outline.heading: Say "the month of Ramadan"
outline.gist: Nothing is dearer to him to speak about than Ramadan. Imam Malik held that one should not say just "Ramadan" but "the month of Ramadan", out of courtesy to this guest who visits once a year.

outline.heading: How Arabs welcome Ramadan
outline.gist: He rarely prefers Arab culture, but here he does: even Arabs far from Allah and the masjid return somewhat to Him when Ramadan comes. He misses the general atmosphere, the honouring of the month and the nasheeds of Tawfiq al-Munajjid and Egypt's Ramadan songs, which soften the heart for what the month brings.

outline.heading: What a nafha is
outline.gist: A nafha is a gift of good, as if carried by the wind: it comes to you, you do not go to it. Ramadan arrives whether you welcome it or not. He prays to reach the month, be among those freed in it, and see relief for the Muslims.

outline.heading: Gift 1: repentance
outline.gist: The door of repentance stays open until the sun rises from the west or the soul reaches the throat, and in Ramadan Allah calls His servants to repent. The companions, taught by the Prophet, prepared their great repentances for great sins to begin with the month.

outline.heading: Ramadan changes the rules of the game
outline.gist: The month turns your life upside down: tarawih, suhoor, Fajr and work leave you barely sleeping. Such radical changes are the best help for dropping bad habits, but they do not build good ones; those need small steady increments, like a hundred tasbih kept for a month before adding another hundred.

outline.heading: A season that cannot be repeated
outline.gist: No one is asked to fast every day or pray every night after Ramadan, and aiming at what you cannot reach hurts you. The gates of Paradise open, Hell's close and the devils are chained; when the month ends that changes, so keep only some good habits, such as two rak'ahs and witr. Ramadan hits your schedule like an earthquake, making it hard to carry on with sins.

outline.heading: A Ramadan day leaves no room for bad habits
outline.gist: He walks through a typical day: suhoor, Fajr, a lesson, Quran, work, an exhausted nap, family and iftar preparations, coming early to the masjid, tarawih on a light stomach, then a bite and collapsing into bed as Nuh settled on the ark. Lived like this, there is no time left for a bad habit.

outline.heading: Name the habit you are leaving
outline.gist: You cannot repent without knowing exactly from what. Sincere repentance names the habit: write it in a notebook, for example which social media platform, how many hours, when and what you watch. Described precisely, it is easy to leave; and every lasting great repentance he knows of began in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Gift 2: fasting, the hardest worship
outline.gist: Given the chance to drop one act of worship, almost the whole ummah would drop fasting. Allah says in a hadith qudsi that the servant leaves his food and desire for His sake, knowing how hard that is, and the Quran says that fasting is good for you.

outline.heading: Good, not better
outline.gist: Ibn Ashur, al-Baydawi and al-Tabari read khayr in "fasting is good for you" as a plain description, not a comparative: fasting is simply excellent for you, in this life and on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Every deed is his except fasting
outline.gist: In the hadith qudsi Allah says every deed of the son of Adam is his except fasting, which is for Him. Prayer varies between focus and showing off, zakat may never fall due if wealth stays below the threshold, and Hajj requires physical, financial and political ability; fasting has no such conditions, and no one can catch you if you eat in secret.

outline.heading: The worship hardest to show off
outline.gist: Only Allah knows whether you fasted, so showing off can hardly enter it; it carries a meaning of sincerity whether you intend it or not. That is why Allah says He Himself rewards it.

outline.heading: Two joys and the gate of al-Rayyan
outline.gist: The fasting person has a joy at breaking the fast and a joy at meeting his Lord, arriving as part of the delegation of the pious. The fasting have their own gate, al-Rayyan, through which every lack in the heart from hardship and poverty is quenched.

outline.heading: Given until satisfied
outline.gist: Allah tells the servant to wish, then reminds him of what he forgot, until the servant says he is satisfied, as in "your Lord will give you and you will be satisfied." You will not grieve over desires you never reached in this life.

outline.heading: Gift 3: the Quran gives Ramadan its rank
outline.gist: The month is honoured because the Quran was sent down in it, on Laylat al-Qadr. Ibn Abbas said it came down to Bayt al-Izza in the lowest heaven that night, the Prophet received "Read in the name of your Lord", and revelation continued for some twenty years.

outline.heading: Al-Zuhri and Malik set hadith aside
outline.gist: When Ramadan came, Imam al-Zuhri, teacher of the great imams, said it is only feeding people and reading Quran. Imam Malik left the hadith gatherings, took off the large cap he wore out of reverence for hadith, and sat with the people of the Quran.

outline.heading: A book for Ramadan: al-Tibyan
outline.gist: If you want to read one book this Ramadan, read al-Nawawi's al-Tibyan on the etiquette of those who carry the Quran. His teacher gave it to him when he memorized, and he has read it since he was fifteen; it is for everyone who carries the Quran in practice, even with only a few surahs memorized.

outline.heading: A khatm in a single rak'ah
outline.gist: Al-Nawawi reports that those who completed the Quran in a single rak'ah are too many to count, among them Uthman, Said ibn Jubayr and Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash. Ibn Asakir completed it weekly and every night in Ramadan; others every two or three nights. Few reach this, but it shows how they honoured the Quran.

outline.heading: Just one khatm
outline.gist: Those who insist on the Prophet's eight rak'ahs can have them as he prayed them: starting at eight and ending at half past three. He recited everything revealed to him many times over in Ramadan. We ask the Muslim community for one khatm in the month: a juz an hour each night, standing.

outline.heading: Not rushed like poetry
outline.gist: Ibn Masud rebuked a man for racing through the Quran like poetry: stop at its wonders and move hearts with it. The Quran is beyond human understanding, so read slowly until its meanings settle in the heart.

outline.heading: Interlude
Gift 4: night prayer
outline.gist: When else would you pray long rak'ahs for an hour or more after Isha? After Ramadan he tries a weekly night prayer and five young men come. In Ramadan Allah drives His servants to His houses, and people who never prayed a sunnah stand with a mushaf for an hour and a half every night.

outline.heading: Eight, thirteen, twenty or more
outline.gist: The Prophet prayed eight rak'ahs, or thirteen in the narrations of Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Khalid in Muslim, which is what they pray here; the Shafi'is made it twenty and the Malikis forty-six, and all is good. What counts is the long standing, listening, the heart and the congregation. The righteous then went home to pray a second khatm, as all his teachers did.

outline.heading: Stay until the imam finishes
outline.gist: Whoever prays with the imam until he finishes is credited with a whole night. The point is to stay to the end of witr, not that the imam should rush; some read it as licence for a quick "demolition tarawih" to settle dinner, which misses the purpose.

outline.heading: The sunnah of tarawih is a khatm
outline.gist: The hadith encourages people to stay, while the imam prays close to the Prophet's prayer. Al-Nawawi in al-Majmu', Ibn Qudamah in al-Mughni, al-Kasani in al-Bada'i and al-Qarafi among the Malikis agree that the sunnah of tarawih is to complete the Quran, once or more as the imam intends; after the khatm it is simply night prayer.

outline.heading: Do not leave before the imam
outline.gist: Once you say Allahu akbar behind him, you are his until he finishes. Leaving the imam mid-prayer without an emergency is a known sign of hypocrisy, which is why most scholars require a traveller behind a resident imam to complete the prayer with him.

outline.heading: Tarawih means rest
outline.gist: Long prayers tire people, so tarawih is named for the rests between sets: drink water, use the washroom, sit. More rak'ahs mean more rests and more khatms; the Malikis of Madinah could complete four or five in the month. Racing through a short surah with takbirs is playing, not tarawih.

outline.heading: Which children to bring
outline.gist: Tarawih is a public sunnah, so bring children to learn. But the Prophet taught that a child brought to the masjid should be able to hold his bladder and his tongue; when the masjid is full, do not bring a toddler you will chase around. Bring school-age children with a mushaf and show them where the khatm is.

outline.heading: Knees for dabke, not for tarawih
outline.gist: In Syria he had constant complaints about the length of prayer and requests for chairs, yet at a wedding the same Abu Riyad would leap through the dabke for hours. People stand and run for hours at sport but cannot stand a little for the One who opened Paradise for them.

outline.heading: Sit rather than leave
outline.gist: For twenty years he has told people to sit if tired; once in Syria he sat while leading and the whole masjid sat with him. Sit for a few rak'ahs rather than go home; a voluntary prayer may even be prayed lying down without excuse. Keep your heart with Allah.

outline.heading: Obligatory prayers outweigh tarawih
outline.gist: Tarawih is honoured as a sunnah special to its season, but Fajr, Isha, Dhuhr, Asr and Maghrib in congregation are greater with Allah. Pray Dhuhr and Asr in the masjid, and break your fast with someone so you pray Maghrib together.

outline.heading: One Fajr outweighs every tarawih
outline.gist: Young men chat for hours after tarawih, then not one comes to Fajr, though he knows they have no school. The reward of one Fajr in congregation exceeds every tarawih from the beginning of time to the Day of Judgment, which no two scholars dispute: nothing brings a servant closer than the obligations, and voluntary deeds then bring Allah's love.

outline.heading: Gift 5: sincerity
outline.gist: There is no time of year when you can better purify your intention, and if you waste it you must wait a year. Allah clears distractions: without food and drink, even socializing loses its point, and you are left with Him.

outline.heading: If not for the rust on the hearts
outline.gist: Shaytan and his whispers are kept away and the gates of Paradise open; only Allah knows what that means. A scholar said that without the rust on the heart, a person would feel the very hour the gate of Paradise opens and the gate of Hell closes.

outline.heading: Ayyub's "cold"
outline.gist: Hammad ibn Zayd said Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, when moved while narrating hadith, would turn away and blow his nose, claiming a cold, to hide his tears.

outline.heading: The follower carries nothing
outline.gist: The imam carries the timing, the length, the verses and their accuracy; the follower is responsible for none of it and can simply listen and enjoy. He has not tasted that in twenty years: even behind a young imam he worries whether he will get it right.

outline.heading: Pause and ask, as the Prophet did
outline.gist: Enjoy Allah's words and look for your heart in them. Ibn Masud and Hudhayfah described the Prophet stopping at verses of bliss to ask for Paradise and at verses of the Fire to seek refuge. Behind the imam, when a verse moves you, speak to your Lord quietly; among hundreds no one sees you.

outline.heading: The drowning do not cling to the drowning
outline.gist: Among those shaded on the Day of Judgment is the one who remembered Allah alone and wept. Many stand alone wishing to be seen, and some stand among millions at Hajj with only Allah in their hearts, knowing the drowning cling only to the One who saves, the Subduer above His servants.

outline.heading: A blessing you do not see
outline.gist: He envies the people praying behind him in Ramadan; he would love to pray at the back with no responsibility while everything that goes wrong lands on the imam. To stand with nothing to do but open your heart to Allah is a blessing you do not see.

outline.heading: Hold on before it is taken
outline.gist: People only see a blessing once it is taken, and it may not return. Use this chance to know yourself and your Lord, open a heart covered with rust and revive a soul dried by distance, and stand surrendered, asking Him to send down His gifts, mercy and freedom from the Fire.

outline.heading: Expose yourselves to His gifts
outline.gist: Your Lord has gifts in the days of your time, so expose yourselves to them: stand where the nafha comes and let it clean what is inside you and light a darkened mind. There is no greater gift than Ramadan, and no one wants to give you more than He does.

outline.heading: The deprived one
outline.gist: Asking to reach the month and not be deprived, he says the deprived one is whoever is denied Allah's mercy in Ramadan. Jibril told the Prophet that humiliated is the one who sees Ramadan come and go without being forgiven, and the Prophet said Ameen.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The whole talk frames Ramadan as five divine gifts that arrive uninvited and must be actively received.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Night prayer and sincerity as the month's last two gifts, and the warning not to let the month pass without forgiveness.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Ramadan is the month for major repentance; the companions planned their big repentances for it, but repentance must name the exact sin.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: Large disruptions help break bad habits, while good habits need small steady increments; do not aim at what you cannot sustain.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Fasting is the act of worship least open to showing off, since no one can check it but Allah.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The fasting person's joy at meeting his Lord, the gate of al-Rayyan, and Allah giving the servant until he is satisfied.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Ramadan's status comes from the Quran; he asks for at least one khatm, read slowly and with reflection, and recommends Nawawi's al-Tibyan.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Tarawih's sunnah, staying with the imam, sitting when tired, and the greater weight of obligatory congregational prayers, especially Fajr.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Ramadan clears distractions so the heart can be sincere; the follower behind the imam can turn wholly to Allah amid a crowd.

themes.label: The Arabic language and its value
themes.note: Arabic's worth lies only in being the language of the Quran and the Prophet; he loves teaching in it and dislikes translating.

quran.point: Quoted humorously for collapsing into bed after a full Ramadan day.
'Fasting is good for you': khayr here is not comparative, per Ibn Ashur, al-Baydawi and al-Tabari.
The pious gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation, for the joy of meeting one's Lord.
Allah will give until the servant is satisfied.
Ramadan's rank comes from the Quran being sent down in it.
The Quran sent down on Laylat al-Qadr, which gives the whole month its standing.
First revelation on the night of al-Qadr.
Allah the Subduer over His servants is the only One the drowning should cling to.

hadith.gist: The door of repentance stays open until the sun rises from the west or the soul reaches the throat.
In Ramadan the gates of Paradise open, the gates of Hell close and the devils are chained.
Hadith qudsi: he leaves his food and desire for My sake.
Hadith qudsi: every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting; it is for Me and I reward it.
The fasting person has two joys: when he breaks his fast and when he meets his Lord; the fasting enter by the gate of al-Rayyan.
Allah tells the servant in Paradise to wish, then reminds him of things he forgot until he says he is satisfied.
Ibn Abbas: the Quran came down to Bayt al-Izza in the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then was revealed over some twenty years.
Ibn Masud rebuked someone for reading the Quran fast like poetry: stop at its wonders and move hearts with it.
The Prophet prayed eight, or thirteen, rak'ahs at night.
hadith.source: Muslim (Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani)

hadith.gist: Whoever prays with the imam until he leaves is credited with standing the whole night.
Hadith qudsi: My servant draws near with nothing dearer to Me than the obligations, and keeps drawing near with voluntary deeds until I love him.
Hudhayfah: the Prophet paused at verses of mercy to ask for Paradise and at verses of punishment to seek refuge.
Among the seven shaded on the Day of Judgment is a man who remembered Allah alone and his eyes overflowed.
Your Lord has gifts (nafahat) in the days of your time, so expose yourselves to them.
Jibril: humiliated is the one who reaches Ramadan and it leaves without his being forgiven; the Prophet said Ameen.

maxims: A nafha comes to you; you do not go to it
Ramadan changes the rules of the game
Big upheavals break bad habits; small steps build good ones
You cannot repent from a habit you have not described
Arabic's value is the value of those who spoke it
The drowning do not cling to the drowning

stories.point: He was slapped for grammar mistakes and had to compose poetry before receiving his ijazah, which is why he loves teaching in Arabic.
Insisted on saying 'Shahr Ramadan' out of courtesy to the month.
In Ramadan they set aside hadith gatherings for feeding people and reading Quran; Malik even removed his hadith cap.

stories.who: Uthman, Said ibn Jubayr, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, Ibn Asakir (via Nawawi's al-Tibyan)
stories.point: The salaf completed the Quran in a single rak'ah or every night in Ramadan, showing how they honoured it.

stories.who: Abu Riyad and men at his Syrian masjid
stories.point: They complained of knee and back pain in tarawih yet danced dabke for hours at weddings.
He once sat while leading and the whole masjid sat with him; sitting is allowed in voluntary prayer.
Pretended to have a cold to hide his tears when moved by hadith, an example of concealed sincerity.

contemporary: Need for Urdu and Bengali religious lessons in the community
Past years' disputes at the masjid over 8 versus 20 tarawih rak'ahs
Youth who stay chatting after tarawih but miss Fajr
Toddlers brought to a crowded masjid during tarawih
Ramadan nasheed culture (Tawfiq al-Munajjid, Egyptian Ramadan songs)
takeaways: Write down the exact bad habit to leave (which app, how many hours, when) and use Ramadan's disruption to drop it.
Complete at least one slow, reflective khatm in Ramadan; consider reading Nawawi's al-Tibyan.
Stay with the imam until he finishes witr, and sit if tired rather than leaving.
Guard obligatory prayers in congregation, especially Fajr, above tarawih.
Bring children who can stay quiet and clean, and use the quiet of Ramadan to purify your intention.

15:85.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَأٓتِيَةࣱۖ فَٱصۡفَحِ ٱلصَّفۡحَ ٱلۡجَمِيلَ
15:85.en: We created not the heavens and the earth and all that is between them save with truth, and lo! the Hour is surely coming. So forgive, (O Muhammad), with a gracious forgiveness

21:18.ar: بَلۡ نَقۡذِفُ بِٱلۡحَقِّ عَلَى ٱلۡبَٰطِلِ فَيَدۡمَغُهُۥ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقࣱۚ وَلَكُمُ ٱلۡوَيۡلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ
21:18.en: Nay, but We hurl the true against the false, and it doth break its head and lo! it vanisheth. And yours will be woe for that which ye ascribe (unto Him)

10:32.ar: فَذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمُ ٱلۡحَقُّۖ فَمَاذَا بَعۡدَ ٱلۡحَقِّ إِلَّا ٱلضَّلَٰلُۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُصۡرَفُونَ
10:32.en: Such then is Allah, your rightful Lord. After the Truth what is there saving error? How then are ye turned away

10:30.ar: هُنَالِكَ تَبۡلُواْ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّآ أَسۡلَفَتۡۚ وَرُدُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَوۡلَىٰهُمُ ٱلۡحَقِّۖ وَضَلَّ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
10:30.en: There doth every soul experience that which it did aforetime, and they are returned unto Allah, their rightful Lord, and that which they used to invent hath failed them

23:71.ar: وَلَوِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلۡحَقُّ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡ لَفَسَدَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَن فِيهِنَّۚ بَلۡ أَتَيۡنَٰهُم بِذِكۡرِهِمۡ فَهُمۡ عَن ذِكۡرِهِم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
23:71.en: And if the Truth had followed their desires, verily the heavens and the earth and whosoever is therein had been corrupted. Nay, We have brought them their Reminder, but from their Reminder they now turn away

41:53.ar: سَنُرِيهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا فِي ٱلۡأٓفَاقِ وَفِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمۡ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّۗ أَوَلَمۡ يَكۡفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
41:53.en: We shall show them Our portents on the horizons and within themselves until it will be manifest unto them that it is the Truth. Doth not thy Lord suffice, since He is Witness over all things

33:4.ar: مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلࣲ مِّن قَلۡبَيۡنِ فِي جَوۡفِهِۦۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزۡوَٰجَكُمُ ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي تُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنۡهُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدۡعِيَآءَكُمۡ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ قَوۡلُكُم بِأَفۡوَٰهِكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهۡدِي ٱلسَّبِيلَ
33:4.en: Allah hath not assigned unto any man two hearts within his body, nor hath He made your wives whom ye declare (to be your mothers) your mothers, nor hath He made those whom ye claim (to be your sons) your sons. This is but a saying of your mouths. But Allah saith the truth and He showeth the way

24:55.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمَا ٱسۡتَخۡلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي ٱرۡتَضَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنࣰ اۚ يَعۡبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:55.en: Allah hath promised such of you as believe and do good work that He will surely make them to succeed (the present rulers) in the earth even as He caused those who were before them to succeed (others); and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He hath approved for them, and will give them in exchange safety after their fear. They serve Me. They ascribe no thing as partner unto Me. Those who disbelieve henceforth, they are the miscreants

7:44.ar: وَنَادَىٰٓ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ أَن قَدۡ وَجَدۡنَا مَا وَعَدَنَا رَبُّنَا حَقࣰّ ا فَهَلۡ وَجَدتُّم مَّا وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمۡ حَقࣰّ اۖ قَالُواْ نَعَمۡۚ فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنُۢ بَيۡنَهُمۡ أَن لَّعۡنَةُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
7:44.en: And the dwellers of the Garden cry unto the dwellers of the Fire: We have found that which our Lord promised us (to be) the Truth. Have ye (too) found that which your Lord promised the Truth? They say: Yea, verily. And a crier in between them crieth: The curse of Allah is on evil-doers

38:84.en: He said: The Truth is, and the Truth I speak

38:85.ar: لَأَمۡلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ وَمِمَّن تَبِعَكَ مِنۡهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
38:85.en: That I shall fill hell with thee and with such of them as follow thee, together

18:56.ar: وَمَا نُرۡسِلُ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَۚ وَيُجَٰدِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ لِيُدۡحِضُواْ بِهِ ٱلۡحَقَّۖ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ ءَايَٰتِي وَمَآ أُنذِرُواْ هُزُوࣰ ا
18:56.en: We send not the messengers save as bearers of good news and warners. Those who disbelieve contend with falsehood in order to refute the Truth thereby. And they take Our revelations and that wherewith they are threatened as a jest

2:119.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرࣰ ا وَنَذِيرࣰ اۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُ عَنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
2:119.en: Lo! We have sent thee (O Muhammad) with the truth, a bringer of glad tidings and a warner. And thou wilt not be asked about the owners of hell-fire

13:17.ar: أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَسَالَتۡ أَوۡدِيَةُۢ بِقَدَرِهَا فَٱحۡتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيۡلُ زَبَدࣰ ا رَّابِيࣰ اۖ وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيۡهِ فِي ٱلنَّارِ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ حِلۡيَةٍ أَوۡ مَتَٰعࣲ زَبَدࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَٱلۡبَٰطِلَۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذۡهَبُ جُفَآءࣰۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمۡكُثُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَالَ
13:17.en: He sendeth down water from the sky, so that valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood beareth (on its surface) swelling foam - from that which they smelt in the fire in order to make ornaments and tools riseth a foam like unto it - thus Allah coineth (the similitude of) the true and the false. Then, as for the foam, it passeth away as scum upon the banks, while, as for that which is of use to mankind, it remaineth in the earth. Thus Allah coineth the similitudes

4:105.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِتَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَلَا تَكُن لِّلۡخَآئِنِينَ خَصِيمࣰ ا
4:105.en: Lo! We reveal unto thee the Scripture with the truth, that thou mayst judge between mankind by that which Allah showeth thee. And be not thou a pleader for the treacherous

4:106.ar: وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرِ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
4:106.en: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

4:107.ar: وَلَا تُجَٰدِلۡ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ خَوَّانًا أَثِيمࣰ ا
4:107.en: And plead not on behalf of (people) who deceive themselves. Lo! Allah loveth not one who is treacherous and sinful

109:2.en: I worship not that which ye worship

109:3.en: Nor worship ye that which I worship

109:4.en: And I shall not worship that which ye worship

109:5.en: Nor will ye worship that which I worship

109:6.en: Unto you your religion, and unto me my religion

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do

xML7KLD10eI.speaker: adnan
xML7KLD10eI.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan Names of Allah series from the previous day's introduction
xML7KLD10eI.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Names of Divine Judgment, Al-Haqq (The Righteous)
xML7KLD10eI.one_line: Al-Haqq as the ultimate value: truth sustains creation, falsehood is passing foam, and believers must live, speak and stand by truth even against themselves.
xML7KLD10eI.summary: Opening the first category, names of divine judgment, he explains Al-Haqq, a root that recurs constantly in the Quran and usually stands alone as a name. Scholars define it as that by which everything exists and functions, the opposite of falsehood, and also the opposite of aimlessness, so it means the Granter of Purpose. Every decision in life weighs truth against desire, fear or interest, and truth should carry infinite weight on that scale. He goes through the Prophet's night prayer supplication, in which Allah, His word, His promise, the meeting with Him, Paradise and the Fire are all called haqq, and shows these in verses. The parable of foam on a flood and scum on molten gold shows falsehood seeming to dominate briefly while what benefits people remains. Falsehood looks strong only when the people of truth fail to raise their banner. The story of the stolen shield, where revelation cleared a Jewish man and exposed a Muslim family, shows truth outranking group loyalty. The Prophet's life was a refusal to compromise even once, because falsehood only needs truth to bend a little. He asks listeners to speak, accept, support, live and if needed die by truth, and to bear witness for justice even against themselves and their families.

outline.heading: Opening
The first category: names of divine judgment
outline.gist: Names pointing to Allah's judgment in this life and on the Day of Judgment; he begins with what he considers the most important of them.

outline.heading: Al-Haqq in the Quran
outline.gist: The word recurs hundreds of times and names Allah nine times, usually alone, otherwise paired with Al-Mubin.

outline.heading: Defining al-haqq
outline.gist: That by which everything exists and without which it collapses; the opposite of falsehood, what lets things function.

outline.heading: Created with truth; truth smashes falsehood
outline.gist: The heavens and earth exist only through truth, and truth strikes falsehood until it vanishes; after truth there is only misguidance.

outline.heading: The Granter of Purpose
outline.gist: Al-Haqq is also the opposite of aimlessness: creation has a purpose and returns to its true Lord.

outline.heading: If truth followed desires
outline.gist: Heavens and earth would collapse if truth followed whims; the dua to see truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood.

outline.heading: The scale of every decision
outline.gist: Life is a test of truth against interest, fear or desire; truth's weight on the scale is infinite and must always win.

outline.heading: The night prayer dua: You are the Truth
outline.gist: The Prophet's supplication calls Allah the Truth; signs in the horizons and in ourselves make clear that He is the Truth.

outline.heading: His word and His promise are truth
outline.gist: Allah speaks the truth and guides the way; the eight statements of the dua are worth memorizing.

outline.heading: The promise to believers and the meeting with Him
outline.gist: Allah promised strength, security and an end to fear for a believing, righteous community, and meeting Him is a certainty.

outline.heading: The people of Paradise call to the Fire
outline.gist: They ask whether the people of the Fire found Allah's promise true, and they admit that they did.

outline.heading: The truth Allah speaks to Iblis; the messengers
outline.gist: Allah answers Iblis's vow by truth that He will fill Hell; messengers bring good news and warning while disbelievers argue with falsehood and mock.

outline.heading: Two surahs, two contrasts
outline.gist: One surah sets truth against falsehood, the other against purposelessness.

outline.heading: The parable of foam and scum
outline.gist: Rain becomes rivers topped with foam, and molten gold is topped with scum; what catches the eye is what floats on top.

outline.heading: Foam vanishes, the beneficial remains
outline.gist: Falsehood seems superior for a moment then disappears, while what benefits people sinks into the earth and gives life.

outline.heading: The people of truth did not raise their banner
outline.gist: Falsehood draws crowds only because those with truth forget to lift their banner or fail to gather around it.

outline.heading: The stolen shield
outline.gist: A Muslim family hid a stolen shield in a Jewish man's yard and nearly had him blamed, until revelation exonerated him and named the true thieves.

outline.heading: Truth trumps all
outline.gist: Revelation cleared someone outside the faith because truth outranks loyalty; the world's turmoil today reflects lost attachment to truth.

outline.heading: Live by it, stand by it, die by it
outline.gist: Speak the truth, accept it on yourself and support it with whatever it requires, even your life.

outline.heading: The Prophet never compromised
outline.gist: Quraysh offered alternating worship, wealth and rule; falsehood needs truth to compromise only once to feel equal.

outline.heading: Truth always holds the upper hand
outline.gist: He even refused a separate gathering for the nobles; whoever has truth has the upper hand, whatever weapons the other side holds.

outline.heading: Which side of the rails do you stand on
outline.gist: Present suffering is foam on top for a while; truth will prevail, in this life or at judgment, so choose your side.

outline.heading: He named Himself after the highest values
outline.gist: Allah took names for the most crucial concepts, Al-Haqq and Al-Adl; living by it means speaking, accepting and supporting truth.

outline.heading: Witnesses for justice even against yourselves
outline.gist: Believers must stand for justice and testify for Allah even against themselves, parents or relatives.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Haqq is the opposite of aimlessness; creation has a purpose.

themes.note: The stolen shield: revelation sided with a Jewish man against Muslim thieves.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: The Prophet refused every compromise; falsehood only needs truth to bend once.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Meeting Allah, Paradise and the Fire are all promised truths.

themes.note: Falsehood's apparent dominance is foam that will pass; the people of truth must raise their banner.
