outline.gist: In the part of the surah on values, He spells out His will because values cannot be accepted without understanding what He intends.

outline.heading: He wants to make things clear to you
outline.gist: The mind is an unmatched tool; once you understand you submit, and once you submit you find fulfilment.

outline.heading: No one commits to what he does not understand
outline.gist: The ummah struggles because we expect commitment without investing in clarity about who Allah is and why He is worth living for.

outline.heading: To guide you in the ways of the prophets before you
outline.gist: You hold a treasure carrying the guidance of Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and the rest, yet spend time on other things.

outline.heading: He wants to turn to you in mercy
outline.gist: When people are wronged they want justice or to see the wrongdoer fall; when you wrong Allah's rights, He wants you to repent and improve.

outline.heading: Even parents want a little punishment
outline.gist: Most parents want their children to reform but with some punishment to feel better; Allah wants no punishment for you.

outline.heading: Those who follow desires want you to deviate entirely
outline.gist: They want you to lose every attachment to this way of life.

outline.heading: He wants to lighten your burden
outline.gist: The fourth wish: a light load so you can carry it, excel and reach your true potential.

outline.heading: 'Where is the ease in fasting and no bars?'
outline.gist: Young people ask where the ease is when they cannot drink, take drugs or have girlfriends; that is exactly where it is.

outline.heading: Ramadan shows how easy you had it
outline.gist: Working without food or sleep reveals how much you had all year and how self-centred you were not to see it.

outline.heading: Following desires is a black hole
outline.gist: It sucks the life out of you until you lose your spirit and identity, anxious about what comes when the lights go out.

outline.heading: The happiest person is the one connected to Allah
outline.gist: Standing in prayer with only Allah in your heart brings a fulfilment so deep that losing a little sends you running back to it.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: An-Nisa' teaches the values behind its laws, and a value is only real when applied to the weak as much as the strong.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Knowing each surah's theme gives direction when reciting and reflecting.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Paradise requires proving yourself: strive in ease and persevere in hardship.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His smile, handshake, full attention and readiness to solve people's problems show the gentleness Allah gave him.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Despite the archers' costly mistake he was told to pardon them and seek forgiveness for them.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Consultation is binding on leaders even after a consultation went wrong; then decide and trust Allah.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Repentance does not entitle you to an easy road; expect repeated falls and remember Allah owes you nothing.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Those killed in Gaza while staying on their land are martyrs, though Muslims mourn rather than celebrate death.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Jabir's father went out at Uhud with rare courage and selflessness and was honoured by his Lord.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Vanity and claiming credit for what Allah gave you are punishable; answer success with humble gratitude.

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Allah states His will: to clarify, to guide in the prophets' ways, to accept repentance and to lighten the burden.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Fasting shows how easy life was all along and where real ease lies.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Desires drain the soul, while connection with Allah gives unmatched happiness.

quran.point: A parallel verse rebuking the assumption of entering Paradise without being tested.
The surah opens with the same idea: people will not be left to say they believe without being tested.

hadith.gist: Recite Al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection shielding and pleading for their companions.
The Prophet would offer his hand first and not withdraw it until the other person did, and he turned his whole body toward whoever he spoke to.
At Uhud the Prophet told the archers not to leave their position even if they saw birds snatching the Muslims' bodies, until he sent for them.
The companions never saw the Prophet weep as he did on the day Hamza was killed.
When Jabir wept over his father, the Prophet said the angels kept shading him with their wings until he was raised.

Allah spoke to Jabir's father without a veil and invited him to wish; he asked to be sent back to be killed again, and when told none return he asked that those behind be informed, so 3:169 was revealed.

maxims: A value used selectively isn't a value
In ease strive, in hardship persevere
Consultation is not optional
Allah owes you nothing
We don't celebrate death; we are comforted
No one commits to what he doesn't understand

stories.point: Their greed caused the defeat, yet the Prophet was told to treat them with tenderness, pardon them and keep consulting them.
He followed the young majority over the elders; after the loss the elders blamed him, but the Quran made consultation binding.
He mourned his uncle all his life, proof that Muslims do not celebrate death.

stories.who: Abdullah, father of Jabir, at Uhud
stories.point: His courage and selflessness earned him Allah speaking to him unveiled and the revelation of 3:169.

contemporary: Gaza: those killed while remaining on their ancestral land counted as martyrs
Some Muslims treating martyrdom as a cause for celebration
Young people seeing alcohol, drugs and relationships as the joys they are denied
takeaways: Work out whether you are in ease or hardship: strive hard in ease and hold your ground in hardship.
Be gentle with people who fail, pardon them, pray for them and keep consulting them.
Do not expect a smooth road after repenting; keep getting up after each fall.
Never claim credit for what Allah gave you; answer success with humble gratitude.
Invest in giving people clarity about Allah and His deen, since no one commits to what he does not understand.

7eqRXRt2MuY.speaker: adnan
7eqRXRt2MuY.speaker_note: mentions his work in Syria and his move to London, Ontario; his usual style; no other speaker named
7eqRXRt2MuY.title: Ramadan: Our Turning Point
7eqRXRt2MuY.one_line: On the eve of Ramadan he blames Gaza's prolonged bloodshed partly on Muslim disorganization, urges a personal turning point, and gives a ten-point Ramadan plan.
7eqRXRt2MuY.summary: Speaking on the last Friday before Ramadan, he asks everyone to enter the month intending to make it a turning point, however many times they have tried before. He grounds that intention in his reading of Gaza: the regime kills freely because it has unconditional Western support, Western leaders give it because they answer only to money and votes, and they feel no pressure because Muslims in the West are disorganized. Muslims lack neither numbers, expertise nor wealth, only organization, having settled into comfortable self-centred lives and petty disputes such as moon sighting. He rejects an end-times passivity that waits for a hero; nobody is coming, and Allah placed each person here with a role. Any explanation of a disaster that leaves out our own shortcomings is not Islamic. He asks listeners to recover the idealistic younger self they once were, as the Prophet revived that spark in his companions, and to bring their regrets to Allah. In the second khutbah he lists ten points: intention, fasting from sin as well as food, congregational prayer and full taraweeh, daily Quran, dhikr, Islamic learning, repairing relationships, service to others, sincere dua, and half an hour of daily life planning.

outline.heading: Opening
One verse, one season, one ummah
outline.gist: The Ramadan verse is being recited on minbars across the Muslim world this week and the next; he finds beauty in Muslims recognising and embracing the same seasons together. On the last Friday before Ramadan he offers thoughts on making the most of it.

outline.heading: Make Ramadan a turning point
outline.gist: His motto: make this Ramadan a turning point, even if you have resolved to change before; there is no limit to how many times. Change on an inner level others cannot see, which will show over time in your decisions and choices. The intention needs a reason, which he grounds in the events of the last 150 days.

outline.heading: 150 days of bloodshed
outline.gist: Some 30,000 civilians killed in 150 days, most of them women and children, in the 21st century while the world watches, and people now being starved: how is this still going on?

outline.heading: Why it continues: unconditional support
outline.gist: The regime would not dare spill so much blood without unconditional support from the world's powers, Canada among them. Had it felt pressure from Western countries it would have held back, sought a deal for its hostages and looked for a ceasefire.

outline.heading: Leaders who worship money and votes
outline.gist: Western governments did not apply pressure because their leaders have no moral compass and worship money, votes and a skewed apocalyptic belief. They felt no pressure at home on re-election or finances, because we are disorganised.

outline.heading: We lack organisation, not numbers or wealth
outline.gist: Muslims in the West lack the financial and political ability to apply pressure, not numbers, expertise or wealth. Decades of colonialism and tyranny left many content with a self-centred life of family, savings, barbecues, cars and vacations.

outline.heading: Muslims were never self-centred
outline.gist: Accepting Islam once made a person alert to the world and outspoken for justice; becoming self-centred cost us the bigger picture. Organisation that changes policy does not happen overnight, since politicians believe only in what keeps them in office.

outline.heading: Too busy arguing about moon sighting
outline.gist: We did not do our job: we argued over moon sighting versus calculation and other petty matters as if we had the luxury, instead of working together and pooling wealth and time even with people we disagree with or dislike, since our interests are one. Part of the ummah paid for it in blood.

outline.heading: So now what?
outline.gist: Will Muslims in the West strengthen their community, give their youth identity, education and confidence, and fund groups that advocate so their voice is heard in policy, or go back to normal once a ceasefire comes? Most of us hold up four or five hands to block out what demands our effort.

outline.heading: The Armageddon mindset: nobody is coming
outline.gist: In Syria he worked against an end-times worldview that waits for prophesied events or for Muslims to become strong again. Nothing is coming, there is no hero on a bus: the people around you are all there is. The Prophet left a generation that dealt with problems personally.

outline.heading: You have a role
outline.gist: We have become a passive ummah asking why someone else does not speak; the only person who should speak is you. Allah put you here with a role; He would not have created you if He did not see something in you.

outline.heading: This will be our turning point
outline.gist: On the eve of Ramadan, intend: I will not go back to the same lifestyle; I will revise my choices, decisions and priorities. When you do, you will find others doing the same.

outline.heading: Fewer people with lesser reasons
outline.gist: You will have companionship; the community still cares, just not yet past the threshold needed to organise and make an impact. The world has been changed by fewer people with lesser reasons, while children die of preventable causes a few miles from help.

outline.heading: Your shortcoming is part of every explanation
outline.gist: Any theory of a disaster that leaves out your own shortcoming is not Islamic; the Quran never lets you look at a bad situation without seeing your share in it. If the mirror shows you a flawless person, you have bigger problems.

outline.heading: Bring back your younger self
outline.gist: Remember the idealistic, hopeful person you were at fifteen or twenty. Life's storms throw you around until you lose your bearings, but that person with the compass still lives inside you; find them and listen to them again.

outline.heading: The Prophet re-ignited his companions
outline.gist: He made people in their forties, fifties and sixties feel young again, kindling what they always knew was inside them under years of clutter, because he lived as that person himself.

outline.heading: Bring your regrets to the One who heals
outline.gist: That version of you is more committed, has more grit, is less selfish and above petty things. Enter Ramadan with it and you will weep over wasted time and mistakes, which is healthy, because you are crying to the One who listens, forgives and heals.

outline.heading: Interlude
Point one: intention
outline.gist: Of ten things to think about in Ramadan, intention comes first; nothing comes close to it in importance. With the right intention things change during the month and after.

outline.heading: Point two: fast from haram, a wider buffer
outline.gist: Fast with excellence: from haram, gossip, and what you should not see, hear or say, not only food and drink. Ramadan pushes the line so even halal food becomes forbidden by day, widening your buffer from haram and bringing your heart closer to Allah.

outline.heading: Point three: congregation and taraweeh to the end
outline.gist: Pray in congregation as a bare minimum and stand with the imam until he finishes taraweeh: we stand an hour and a half in line for food or a driver's licence. Open the Quran and follow along; if tired, sit or take a break and come back. Prayer improves with practice; choose the masjid closest to you and stay for witr and the dua.

outline.heading: Point four: the Quran without a middleman
outline.gist: Revive your relationship with the Quran: recite, memorise, understand. You need no interpreter between you and Allah; read a little every day. This book saved us and will save us again; until we return to it we stay lost.

outline.heading: Point five: dhikr in the hungry hours
outline.gist: When you are starving with a headache, instead of scrolling, say words that connect you to Allah and learn to find joy in His names.

outline.heading: Point six: Islamic knowledge
outline.gist: Invest in your Islamic understanding, not only academic education: attend a daily or weekly dars and keep it after Ramadan. He admits he now feels ashamed eating while people in Gaza fight over wheat; change starts with the spark Ramadan lights inside you, which later becomes advocacy, outreach and giving.

outline.heading: Point seven: repair relationships
outline.gist: Invest in your spouse and parents, call people you have not spoken to in years and mend broken relationships; the ummah cannot survive divided.

outline.heading: Point eight: service, rewarded twice
outline.gist: Serve others whether or not they appreciate it: sadaqah, helping the masjid run, minding children so others can pray. If you would otherwise be praying or reciting, you earn the reward of both, the best deal in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Point nine: the art of dua
outline.gist: Allah speaks to you through a book, so learn to converse with Him. Drop the formal job-interview dua with titles and signatures; speak to Him as you are, as creation to Creator.

outline.heading: Point ten: half an hour of planning a day
outline.gist: Put the phone away for thirty minutes a day and write who you hope to be, what you stand for and what legacy you will leave. The plan will almost always fail, but its skeleton keeps you yourself when life throws curveballs: fifteen years ago he had not even heard of London, Ontario. Especially for high school and university students.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: Enter every Ramadan intending it to be a turning point; there is no limit to how many times one can resolve to change.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward
themes.note: Western Muslims cannot pressure politicians because they are disorganized; they must fund and build advocacy groups so their voice is heard and respected in policy.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Muslims must pool wealth and time and work together even when they disagree or dislike one another, because their interests are one.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Rejecting end-times waiting, he insists no hero is coming; Allah created each person with a role and believes in them, so they must fulfil it.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Any theory of a crisis that omits your own shortcoming is un-Islamic; look in the mirror and recover the idealistic person you once were.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: A ten-point plan for the month: intention, fasting from sin, congregational and taraweeh prayer, Quran, dhikr, knowledge, relationships, service, dua and daily planning.

themes.note: Thirty minutes a day of planning and journaling about legacy and values gives a skeleton of identity that survives life's curveballs, even when plans fail.

stories.point: He spent years challenging an apocalyptic worldview that made people wait for prophesied events instead of acting.
He re-ignited the youthful idealism already inside people in their forties to sixties, giving them something to live for.

Canada and Western governments' unconditional support for Israel
Moon sighting versus calculation debate over the start of Ramadan

11:6.ar: ۞وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رِزۡقُهَا وَيَعۡلَمُ مُسۡتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسۡتَوۡدَعَهَاۚ كُلࣱّ فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
11:6.en: And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah. He knoweth its habitation and its repository. All is in a clear Record

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

2:126.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ ٱجۡعَلۡ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا ءَامِنࣰ ا وَٱرۡزُقۡ أَهۡلَهُۥ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ مِنۡهُم بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُۥ قَلِيلࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَضۡطَرُّهُۥٓ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلنَّارِۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
2:126.en: And when Abraham prayed: My Lord! Make this a region of security and bestow upon its people fruits, such of them as believe in Allah and the Last Day, He answered: As for him who disbelieveth, I shall leave him in contentment for a while, then I shall compel him to the doom of Fire - a hapless journey's end

41:10.ar: وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ مِن فَوۡقِهَا وَبَٰرَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقۡوَٰتَهَا فِيٓ أَرۡبَعَةِ أَيَّامࣲ سَوَآءࣰ لِّلسَّآئِلِينَ
41:10.en: He placed therein firm hills rising above it, and blessed it and measured therein its sustenance in four Days, alike for (all) who ask

30:40.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ رَزَقَكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمۡ ثُمَّ يُحۡيِيكُمۡۖ هَلۡ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُم مَّن يَفۡعَلُ مِن ذَٰلِكُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
30:40.en: Allah is He Who created you and then sustained you, then causeth you to die, then giveth life to you again. Is there any of your (so-called) partners (of Allah) that doeth aught of that? Praised and Exalted be He above what they associate (with Him)

34:39.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُ لَهُۥۚ وَمَآ أَنفَقۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَهُوَ يُخۡلِفُهُۥۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلرَّٰزِقِينَ
34:39.en: Say: Lo! my Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will of His bondmen, and narroweth (it) for him. And whatsoever ye spend (for good) He replaceth it. And He is the Best of Providers

14:32.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ لِتَجۡرِيَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ
14:32.en: Allah is He Who created the heavens and the earth, and causeth water to descend from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you, and maketh the ships to be of service unto you, that they may run upon the sea at His command, and hath made of service unto you the rivers

14:33.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ دَآئِبَيۡنِۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ
14:33.en: And maketh the sun and the moon, constant in their courses, to be of service unto you, and hath made of service unto you the night and the day

14:34.ar: وَءَاتَىٰكُم مِّن كُلِّ مَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُۚ وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحۡصُوهَآۗ إِنَّ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ لَظَلُومࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
14:34.en: And He giveth you of all ye ask of Him, and if ye would count the bounty of Allah ye cannot reckon it. Lo! man is verily a wrong-doer, an ingrate

29:17.ar: إِنَّمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡثَٰنࣰ ا وَتَخۡلُقُونَ إِفۡكًاۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لَكُمۡ رِزۡقࣰ ا فَٱبۡتَغُواْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرِّزۡقَ وَٱعۡبُدُوهُ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لَهُۥٓۖ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
29:17.en: Ye serve instead of Allah only idols, and ye only invent a lie. Lo! those whom ye serve instead of Allah own no provision for you. So seek your provision from Allah, and serve Him, and give thanks unto Him, (for) unto Him ye will be brought back

2:172.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِلَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
2:172.en: O ye who believe! Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and render thanks to Allah if it is (indeed) He Whom ye worship

51:22.en: And in the heaven is your providence and that which ye are promised

51:23.ar: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقࣱّ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمۡ تَنطِقُونَ
51:23.en: And by the Lord of the heavens and the earth, it is the truth, even as (it is true) that ye speak

63:10.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
63:10.en: And spend of that wherewith We have provided you before death cometh unto one of you and he saith: My Lord! If only thou wouldst reprieve me for a little while, then I would give alms and be among the righteous

15:20.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا لَكُمۡ فِيهَا مَعَٰيِشَ وَمَن لَّسۡتُمۡ لَهُۥ بِرَٰزِقِينَ
15:20.en: And we have given unto you livelihoods therein, and unto those for whom ye provide not

67:21.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرۡزُقُكُمۡ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَ رِزۡقَهُۥۚ بَل لَّجُّواْ فِي عُتُوࣲّ وَنُفُورٍ
67:21.en: Or who is he that will provide for you if He should withhold His providence? Nay, but they are set in pride and frowardness

nOdfk1yNrEg.speaker: adnan
nOdfk1yNrEg.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan Names of Allah series, moving to the category of provision
nOdfk1yNrEg.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Names of Provision, Al-Razzaq (The Provider)
nOdfk1yNrEg.one_line: Al-Razzaq: everything you have is provision decreed for you, tied in the Quran to need, gratitude, certainty and giving; starvation comes from withheld shares.
nOdfk1yNrEg.summary: He distinguishes Al-Razzaq, the One who provides continuously to all without exception, from the less intensive Ar-Raziq, and defines rizq as anything usable. Rizq becomes a blessing (ni'mah) only when you recognize it as one, so the difference is in your perspective, and everything from your skin colour to your community is rizq. Every creature's provision is upon Allah; Ibrahim's prayer for Mecca was corrected to include disbelievers, and a story has Ibrahim rebuked for evicting a disbelieving guest whom Allah had fed for seventy years. Provisions were measured before humans existed, and no soul dies before using up its share. In the Quran rizq is tied to four ideas: it follows need rather than want, it calls for gratitude that means using it as Allah wants, it is certain enough that Allah swears by it, and it must be given before death brings regret. Rizq includes time, knowledge and attention, not just money. The sardine run and a drop of water travelling the globe to your mouth illustrate decreed provision. People starve because their share sits in others' hands, as with unpaid zakat, and there is enough food for all but not for greed. He asks people to never compromise for rizq, earn only halal, be content while working hard, and become a source of provision for others.

outline.heading: Al-Razzaq versus Ar-Raziq
outline.gist: The intensive form means continuous provision to all without exception, while the simple form carries no such sense.

outline.heading: What rizq means
outline.gist: Rizq is anything usable, even if not beneficial; he asks what separates rizq from ni'mah.

outline.heading: Rizq becomes ni'mah when you see it
outline.gist: The only difference is perspective: acknowledging provision as a blessing makes it ni'mah.

outline.heading: Everything you were given is rizq
outline.gist: Skin, height, parents, birthplace, friends and community are all provision; how much you recognize as blessing depends on you.

outline.heading: Provision is upon Allah
outline.gist: Understand at least each category of names; no creature on earth except that its provision is Allah's responsibility.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's prayer for the barren valley
outline.gist: Ibrahim left his family by the sacred house so they would pray, asking that people come to them and fruits sustain them.

outline.heading: The house existed before Ibrahim
outline.gist: He named the sacred house before building it, because Adam had built it and Ibrahim only rebuilt it.

outline.heading: Provision for disbelievers too
outline.gist: Ibrahim asked fruits for believers only; Allah corrected him that He provides for those who disbelieve as well.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and the disbelieving guest
outline.gist: Ibrahim threw out an old man who denied God; Allah rebuked him for refusing one night to someone He had fed for seventy years.

outline.heading: Provisions measured before creation
outline.gist: Allah assigned the earth's sustenance before humans existed; He creates, provides, causes death and gives life, which no partner can do.

outline.heading: No soul dies before its provision ends
outline.gist: Jibril inspired the Prophet that no soul dies until it has used up all the provision decreed for it.

outline.heading: Rizq written in the womb
outline.gist: The angel who breathes the soul into the fetus writes its provision among four decrees.

outline.heading: First theme: what you need, not what you want
outline.gist: Allah extends and restricts provision for His servant's sake; abundance and scarcity are both for your benefit.

outline.heading: Second theme: gratitude
outline.gist: Hamd is saying alhamdulillah; shukr is using what you were given in the way that pleases Allah and benefits others.

outline.heading: Countless blessings, little gratitude
outline.gist: Heavens, rain, ships, sun, moon and night were subjected for us; seek provision only from Allah and eat of the good and thank Him.

outline.heading: Third theme: certainty
outline.gist: Your provision is in the heavens and Allah swears it is true; a bedouin asked what people did to make the Generous One swear.

outline.heading: Fourth theme: giving before death
outline.gist: Give before you wish on your deathbed to return and give; rizq includes knowledge, time, expertise and listening.

outline.heading: Seeing yourself through a lens of poverty
outline.gist: If your bank account is your most valuable possession you have made yourself poor; the dead wish they had given time, service and emotion.

outline.heading: The sardine run
outline.gist: Sardines swim the same route every year to be eaten by predators that wait for them: provision for those you do not provide for.

outline.heading: A drop of water with your name on it
outline.gist: A drop evaporates over the Pacific, rains on Europe's mountains, is bottled and shipped to Canada, and ends up in your mouth because it was decreed.

outline.heading: Why do people starve?
outline.gist: No one provides if Allah withholds, yet famine and war starvation happen because Allah placed their provision in others' hands.

outline.heading: Zakat is someone else's provision
outline.gist: After a lunar year part of your wealth belongs to others; holding it back withholds their rizq, and you will answer for it.

outline.heading: Enough for bellies, not for greed
outline.gist: There is enough food for many times our numbers; starvation in hard times comes from people holding back each other's provision.

outline.heading: First: never compromise for rizq
outline.gist: Do not fear for your provision or give up who you are for it; bring only halal into your home and your children's bodies.

outline.heading: The provider's job; contentment and hard work
outline.gist: Allah provides, a man's job is to ensure it is halal; be content with what you get while working hard and asking for more.

outline.heading: Halal earnings and accepted dua; be someone's provision
outline.gist: The man who raises his hands while eating and dressing in haram is not answered; give from what you receive and be a source of provision.

outline.heading: Refuge from disbelief and poverty
outline.gist: The Prophet paired them in his dua because it is hard to speak of God to the starving, and poverty comes from human greed.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Razzaq as continuous provider to all, and rizq as everything decreed for you.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Rizq becomes blessing only when you recognize it.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Shukr means using provision as Allah wants, not just saying alhamdulillah.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Provision is sworn by Allah and certain; do not fear for it.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Give from all forms of rizq before death brings regret.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Zakat is others' provision held in your wealth; starvation results from withheld shares and greed.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: Provision follows need, and both abundance and scarcity serve you.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Earn only halal, be content while working hard, and do not compromise yourself for money.
