2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: (Fast) a certain number of days; and (for) him who is sick among you, or on a journey, (the same) number of other days; and for those who can afford it there is a ransom: the feeding of a man in need - but whoso doeth good of his own accord, it is better for him: and that ye fast is better for you if ye did but know

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who findeth not (the wherewithal), let him fast for two successive months before they touch one another; and for him who is unable to do so (the penance is) the feeding of sixty needy ones. This, that ye may put trust in Allah and His messenger. Such are the limits (imposed by Allah); and for disbelievers is a painful doom

19:8.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَٰمࣱ وَكَانَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتِي عَاقِرࣰ ا وَقَدۡ بَلَغۡتُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِبَرِ عِتِيࣰّ ا
19:8.en: He said: My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached infirm old age

24:60.ar: وَٱلۡقَوَٰعِدُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّٰتِي لَا يَرۡجُونَ نِكَاحࣰ ا فَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَن يَضَعۡنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ غَيۡرَ مُتَبَرِّجَٰتِۭ بِزِينَةࣲۖ وَأَن يَسۡتَعۡفِفۡنَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُنَّۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:60.en: As for women past child-bearing, who have no hope of marriage, it is no sin for them if they discard their (outer) clothing in such a way as not to show adornment. But to refrain is better for them. Allah is Hearer, Knower

aBuc4AC7NmU.speaker: adnan
aBuc4AC7NmU.speaker_note: speaks of growing up and studying medicine in Arabic in Syria, his shaykhs' ijazah, ER work, and this masjid's tent and zakat policy
aBuc4AC7NmU.title: Ramadan Prep Series: The Fiqh of Fasting
aBuc4AC7NmU.one_line: A practical fiqh walk-through of Ramadan fasting: intention, nullifiers, disputed medical cases, concessions, expiations, sunnahs, tarawih and zakat al-fitr.
aBuc4AC7NmU.summary: He opens with a lament for the decline of Arabic, tying it to the fall of Syria as its stronghold and recounting his own rigorous training, and argues that the Quran and the Arabic language preserve each other. He then teaches the fiqh of fasting from slides. Ramadan fasting needs an intention from the night before, though waking for suhoor counts, and the Maliki view allows one intention for the month. He gives one rule for nullifiers: anything deliberately taken into the body that nourishes. He lists clear nullifiers and non-nullifiers, then his own views on disputed cases: inhalers, drops and non-nutritive IV lines do not break the fast, suppositories do. He explains the concessions (illness, travel, pregnancy and nursing, severe exhaustion), stresses that harming the body to fast is sinful, and sets out the major and minor expiations with dollar estimates. A long aside rebukes misuse of zakat, including masjids taking it. He closes with sunnahs of suhoor and iftar, fasting from sins, staying with the imam in tarawih, and flexible rulings on zakat al-fitr and the Eid prayer.

outline.heading: Arabic, nearly a thing of the past
outline.gist: No nafha in the year compares with Ramadan, and he wants a talk or two on it in Arabic to honour both the month and the language of the Quran, which has become almost a relic even in Arab lands. Scholars in Morocco, Mauritania, Kuwait and Egypt have recently raised the alarm.

outline.heading: Syria, the fallen stronghold
outline.gist: One cause is the fall of Arabic's stronghold, Syria, a country that loves the language and teaches every science in it. He studied all of medicine in Arabic and took years to learn the English terms.

outline.heading: Classical Arabic or a beating
outline.gist: As a boy his shaykh made them preach to trees, stones and animals. At school, in military uniform, answers had to be in classical Arabic; his teacher Omar al-Sabbagh spoke nothing else and punished any answer in dialect.

outline.heading: The Alfiyyah by page number
outline.gist: All his teachers mastered the arts of Arabic. He studied Ibn Malik's Alfiyyah with Ibn Aqil's commentary before university, and one of his scholars, who never attended school, knew the Alfiyyah and its commentaries by page number.

outline.heading: No ijazah without poetry
outline.gist: A hafiz holding an ijazah had to master Arabic, prosody and poetry: his shaykh would not sign his Quran ijazah until he composed classical verse. When the stronghold fell, that care declined, and the ummah must revive it.

outline.heading: Scripture only in translation
outline.gist: We revive Arabic not for itself but for the Quran, which cannot be understood without it. The Gospel was revealed to Isa in Hebrew, rendered into Greek, then Latin, then other languages, and no original remains.

outline.heading: A 1,400-year-old book you can still read
outline.gist: Try reading anything written in English, French or German in the sixth century; those languages have changed beyond recognition. With basic Arabic you can read and understand a 1,400-year-old book: the Quran preserved the language and the language preserved the Quran.

outline.heading: Intention: a voluntary fast can start late
outline.gist: He speaks of intention as fiqh, not as Ihsan. A voluntary fast needs no intention from the night: if you wake near noon having eaten nothing and decide to fast, it is accepted with the reward of the whole day.

outline.heading: Ramadan needs an intention from the night
outline.gist: For Ramadan the intention must be set the night before. For the Shafi'is that is every night, though it need not be spoken; waking for suhoor is itself the intention. Someone who forgot it was Ramadan and remembered after Fajr has no valid fast.

outline.heading: Malik: one intention for the month
outline.gist: To escape that strictness, Imam Malik allows one intention before Ramadan to cover the whole month. It is not complicated: if you know tomorrow is Ramadan and you will fast, you have intended, and forgetfully eating during the day is a gift from Allah.

outline.heading: One rule for what breaks the fast
outline.gist: Anything you deliberately take into your body that provides nourishment, in the medical sense, breaks the fast. Understand this rule and you are spared most questions.

outline.heading: The same questions every year
outline.gist: Every Ramadan people ask as if it were humanity's first: toothbrushing, eye drops, the same questions for fifteen years. Learn the fiqh of Ramadan once, settle on it, and share it, so the shaykhs do not come to dread the month.

outline.heading: Nullifier: deliberate eating and drinking
outline.gist: Eating or drinking on purpose, including deliberately swallowing water during wudu. Deliberateness is an intention only Allah sees; no one can judge your fast for you, it is between you and Him.

outline.heading: Nullifier: intercourse and ejaculation
outline.gist: Intercourse, or deliberately reaching climax, breaks the fast and requires an expiation as well as a make-up day. A wet dream during a daytime nap does not; just bathe and continue, and waking after the Fajr adhan without having bathed is no problem.

outline.heading: Nullifier: induced vomiting
outline.gist: Deliberately making yourself vomit breaks the fast; vomiting that simply happens does not. A sick person already has an excuse not to fast.

outline.heading: Nullifier: IV nutrition and blood
outline.gist: A saline drip or a blood transfusion breaks the fast. In illness that is excused, but doing it without cause would be a sin.

outline.heading: Nullifier: smoking
outline.gist: Any kind of smoking breaks the fast: cigarettes, shisha or a pipe.

outline.heading: Nullifier: menstruation and postnatal bleeding
outline.gist: If bleeding begins during the day, that day's fast is void and is made up later. These are the six well-known nullifiers.

outline.heading: Not a nullifier: toothbrushing
outline.gist: Brushing with paste, a miswak or an electric brush does not break the fast, unless you swallow the paste or water.

outline.heading: Not a nullifier: eating forgetfully
outline.gist: Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully was fed and given drink by Allah. Out of courtesy, let him finish his mouthful rather than remind him, though a fasting onlooker may be tempted by envy; once he remembers he must spit out what is in his mouth. Someone laying out a whole meal is another matter.

outline.heading: Not a nullifier: non-nutritive injections
outline.gist: A wet dream in sleep is natural. Intramuscular or subcutaneous injections that carry no nourishment, such as painkillers, antibiotics or vitamin B12, do not break the fast; insulin he discusses separately.

outline.heading: Not a nullifier: swallowing saliva
outline.gist: Swallowing saliva does not break the fast even if a lot gathers, though deliberately collecting it is disliked and unpleasant.

outline.heading: Not a nullifier: water left after wudu
outline.gist: Rinse your mouth in wudu as usual; the sunnah of exaggerated rinsing does not apply while fasting. Water that remains despite normal rinsing does no harm, but do not multiply wudu for its own sake.

outline.heading: Disputed: inhalers
outline.gist: He moves from agreed cases to disputed ones. Scholars differ, but he holds that an inhaler for asthma, COPD or another lung disease does not break the fast.

outline.heading: Disputed: eye and ear drops
outline.gist: Although some may reach inside, drops in the eye or ear, antibiotic or otherwise, do not break the fast in his view.

outline.heading: Disputed: non-nutritive IV lines
outline.gist: He changed his view last year: an IV antibiotic without saline does not break the fast in his view, though most scholars hold that anything entering a vein does. Someone receiving such treatment is usually too ill to fast anyway.

outline.heading: Dialysis patients should not fast
outline.gist: Someone on dialysis two or three times a week should not fast at all, given the harm and the fluids he needs during the day; he pays the expiation instead, and even after a transplant may never be able to fast. Preserving the body comes first here.

outline.heading: Suppositories, and erring on the safe side
outline.gist: Of the four disputed cases, he holds that inhalers and drops do not break the fast, while IV lines are case by case. Suppositories, he thinks, do break it, since anything entering either passage does, though some scholars disagree for antibiotic or haemorrhoid suppositories. Take the view you find sound; if ill, take the concession, and when in doubt count the day broken and make it up.

outline.heading: Concession: illness
outline.gist: Whoever is ill or travelling makes up the days later, and sometimes breaking the fast is obligatory because continuing would harm the sick person.

outline.heading: Harming the body is a sin
outline.gist: People hate breaking their fast in Ramadan, but if your doctor says fasting harms you, break it. Making yourself sicker to fast is wrong and sinful: the body is a trust, and you were not required to fast.

outline.heading: Concession: travel, stricter than prayer
outline.gist: Scholars are lenient on combining and shortening prayers even for short trips, but stricter about breaking the fast. To stay clear of the dispute, take the longest distance cited, about 82 kilometres.

outline.heading: Travel: how many days
outline.gist: The schools differ: three days for the Shafi'is and Hanbalis, perhaps a week for the Malikis, two weeks for Abu Hanifa. Ask before travelling, and avoid breaking unless needed, since many missed days are hard to make up; perhaps break only on the days of travel.

outline.heading: Concession: pregnancy and nursing
outline.gist: A pregnant or nursing woman may break her fast, but owes a fidyah for each day even if she makes it up within the year.

outline.heading: Concession: severe exhaustion
outline.gist: Ramadan is easier now that it falls in spring and winter, but in summer a labourer carrying loads up stairs in the heat should intend to fast each day and break only when exhaustion overwhelms him. Even if that happens every day of the month, there is no sin as long as he intended each morning.

outline.heading: Northern Europe's endless days
outline.gist: Brothers in Germany and Scandinavia during summer Ramadans had only three or four hours of night. He told them to intend the fast and break it when they could no longer work or study, then make it up. Other views, fasting by the nearest normal region or by Makkah, are not needed where we live.

outline.heading: You know yourself
outline.gist: Whether exhaustion has reached the point of harm or of failing your duties is between you and Allah, so there is no need to ask him: you know yourself. These are the four concessions.

outline.heading: Make up before next Ramadan
outline.gist: Missed days must be made up before the next Ramadan. Sisters who miss a week or the whole month through pregnancy or nursing often remember thirty days before; days still owed when Ramadan arrives must still be made up, plus a fidyah, which may be given to the poor in any country.

outline.heading: The major expiation, in order
outline.gist: Breaking the fast by intercourse requires the major expiation, in order: free a slave; if not, fast sixty consecutive days; if unable, feed sixty poor people.

outline.heading: Sixty days, or $1,200
outline.gist: He recently learned of someone who fell into this, fasted sixty consecutive days and benefited enormously. Feeding sixty means a full, satisfying meal each, about $20 today, so roughly $1,200. He teases couples who ignore each other all year and only find each other on a Ramadan afternoon.

outline.heading: Deliberate ejaculation
outline.gist: Far more common among young men is deliberate ejaculation. Most scholars do not require the major expiation for it, only repentance and a make-up day, though there is no harm in someone choosing to do it by analogy, as some young men have.

outline.heading: Deliberate eating, a major expiation too
outline.gist: All agree intercourse requires the major expiation; the schools are split over deliberate eating and drinking. He holds it deserves it even more, as when someone breaks his fast in a fit of anger: free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, and the $1,200 will hurt.

outline.heading: The minor expiation and chronic illness
outline.gist: The minor expiation is feeding one poor person for each day, the fidyah of the verse. It is for chronic illness such as dialysis or diabetes; insulin under the skin does not break the fast in his view, but depending on the type of diabetes, fasting may put a patient in a coma.

outline.heading: Elderly diabetics in the emergency room
outline.gist: During his hospital years, elderly women with diabetes who insisted on fasting arrived late at night with dangerously low or high sugar. Advice goes in one ear and out the other; the best thing is a son who calls him to talk to his mother.

outline.heading: Six hundred dollars to feed the hungry
outline.gist: A chronically ill person simply multiplies: thirty meals at $20 is $600, paid at once to feed the poor. This masjid does not collect zakat or expiations, but many others run feeding programs, and half the Muslim world is hungry. It must go to feeding, not to building a hospital; charity covers those.

outline.heading: Not to your parents or children
outline.gist: Zakat cannot go to your parents or children, since it would return to you as inheritance. Pay the dues in their channels and give your family from your own money; even the Arabs of jahiliyyah were more generous than people who calculate exactly what they owe.

outline.heading: Why this masjid refuses zakat
outline.gist: Every year someone offers his company's zakat of seventy or a hundred thousand, though the masjid barely survives and its tent alone cost $20,000. He does not see it as permissible for masjids to take zakat, though others hold differently.

outline.heading: Zakat's prescribed channels
outline.gist: Zakat goes to its recipients: the poor, the needy and those who work on it. If you personally find the poor and distribute it you may keep at most a tenth, but not if you pass it to a charity. Most must go to the poor and needy; give as Allah ordered, then give from your own wealth. Cash given with the intention of feeding is fine.

outline.heading: Fidyah for the elderly
outline.gist: The elderly need not be ill: whoever has reached extreme old age may break the fast and pay fidyah, as in the fiqh of the elderly and of women past childbearing. Some scholars say a child with means should pay for a parent. There is no fixed age; it depends on custom and strength.

outline.heading: One fidyah per missed day
outline.gist: Whoever delays a make-up past the next Ramadan owes one fidyah per day, not one for every year it is delayed; sisters with fasts owed since 1998 need not bankrupt their husbands. They make up the days, and the delay is a sin requiring repentance, graver than the expiation.

outline.heading: Nursing and pregnant women
outline.gist: A pregnant or nursing woman may break her fast, but owes the minor expiation even if she makes the days up before next Ramadan: break, pay the fidyah right away, and make up the day.

outline.heading: A day no lifetime can replace
outline.gist: A Ramadan day broken without excuse cannot be made up by fasting a lifetime, as the Prophet said. You still fast a day in its place, but the reward lost cannot be recovered; with an excuse you lose nothing. That is how Allah honours the obligation. He lists again who owes the minor expiation.

outline.heading: Do not drink like a camel
outline.gist: Delay suhoor as the hadith says, but drinking huge amounts helps only if you have a hump; you just spend the day in the washroom. A few litres spread out is enough: one in the morning, one at iftar, one and a half at night, unless you are an athlete or have a condition.

outline.heading: Salt and sugar call for water
outline.gist: Salty snacks at suhoor will kill you by midday: salts and sugars draw water by osmosis, so the more of them you eat, the more you must drink. Keep suhoor moderate.

outline.heading: Suhoor for its blessing
outline.gist: Eat suhoor for the blessing the Prophet taught. His suhoor, like his iftar, was a few dates, water and perhaps milk; you need nothing more. He marvels at families cooking every dish for an hour and a half before Fajr.

outline.heading: Hasten iftar, delay suhoor: no extra zeal
outline.gist: Do not delay iftar. Adding unprescribed devotion is the essence of bid'ah: the fast is Fajr to Maghrib, not two hours either side, so take your last bite just before the adhan and break the fast at once. The Prophet commanded ease, not exaggeration.

outline.heading: Break on fresh dates
outline.gist: The sunnah is to break the fast on fresh dates, or dry dates if there are none, or water; other food is fine, but never a cigarette or a sin.

outline.heading: The dua at iftar
outline.gist: The fasting person's dua at iftar is not rejected. Whether you make it just before or just after breaking the fast is a verbal difference not worth arguing over.

outline.heading: Fast from sins too
outline.gist: Fasting from the lawful while cursing, backbiting, fighting, looking at and eating the forbidden makes no sense: whoever does not abandon false speech and acting on it, Allah has no need for him to leave his food and drink.

outline.heading: Young people, pray it in full
outline.gist: Not strictly fiqh of fasting, but pray tarawih in full, especially if you are young, in a masjid that completes the Quran, with a mushaf open. People queue for hours for a certificate, and back pain only seems to strike in tarawih, never at the dabke.

outline.heading: Leave with the imam
outline.gist: Getting into the habit young matters. In the Prophet's era leaving before the imam finished was a sign of hypocrisy; today someone with work in the morning may leave, but without an excuse stay to the end, the greatest reward of prayer in Ramadan.

outline.heading: The number carries no weight
outline.gist: Twenty, twelve, eight or forty-six: whoever thinks the number is a problem has not read fiqh, and the imams differed on it. What matters is how much Quran is recited. Insist on the Prophet's eight rak'ahs and we start at eight and finish at three.

outline.heading: The sunnah is a khatm
outline.gist: The Prophet recited what had been revealed many times over in Ramadan. Al-Nawawi in al-Majmu' says the sunnah is at least one khatm, and tarawih's sunnah ends with the khatm the imam intended. They pray ten plus three here, following two sound hadiths, from Zayd ibn Khalid in Muslim and Ibn Abbas in Bukhari.

outline.heading: Pray it in the masjid
outline.gist: The number lets people leave in time for work while hearing the whole Quran without exhausting rak'ahs. Home and masjid are both valid, but he prefers the masjid, since at home laziness wins the first time the father has a headache. Commit to a masjid that completes the Quran and come early.

outline.heading: Bound to the imam
outline.gist: Tarawih is named for the rest between its sets. Once you say Allahu akbar behind the imam you are bound until he finishes. Ibn Masud admitted he once intended something bad, to leave the Prophet in prayer, and the man who left Mu'adh's long Isha was said to have become a hypocrite.

outline.heading: Rest or sit, but do not leave
outline.gist: The imam stands straight up for the next set, but you may rest for two rak'ahs in your place or pray sitting, which earns reward. That is far better than praying four or six and walking out.

outline.heading: Zakat al-fitr in cash
outline.gist: People love to fight every year over paying zakat al-fitr in cash. The Hanafis allowed it long ago, and every school has a view permitting it; give a sa' of dates, barley or wheat, or cash, as you prefer. The matter is broad.

outline.heading: Give it about a week early
outline.gist: It must be paid before the Eid prayer, and may be paid days or a week before, after mid-month as the Shafi'is say, or from the start of Ramadan. He prefers about a week early so it reaches families in time for their children to enjoy Eid; it is roughly $15 to $20 a person.

outline.heading: For everyone you support, even the unborn
outline.gist: The provider pays for those he supports: wife, children, and parents if he supports them; a father may still pay for an independent son as extra good. It is also paid for a fetus past 120 days, when the soul is breathed in, as Imam Ahmad and others hold.

outline.heading: The Eid prayer: later is fine, one gathering
outline.gist: Go out to the Eid prayer with your family, outdoors. Eid al-Fitr may be delayed toward midday if that is easier for people. The sunnah is one gathering in one or two places, not sixty separate Eids; the Prophet took the whole town out with families and even their animals.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Jurisprudence rulings and how to approach fiqh
themes.note: A systematic fiqh lesson; he gives a single governing rule for nullifiers and his own reasoned positions where scholars differ.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Rulings of the Ramadan fast from intention to tarawih, framed as preparation for the coming month.

themes.label: The Arabic language and its value
themes.note: Arabic must be revived not for ethnic pride but because the Quran is understood only through it.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Dialysis patients should not fast and the sick who harm their bodies by fasting are sinful; the body is a trust.

themes.label: Visiting the sick, caring for elders and the vulnerable
themes.note: Elderly diabetics who insist on fasting end up in emergency; families should persuade them to take the concession and pay fidyah.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Zakat and expiations have fixed recipients; masjids should not take zakat, it cannot go to parents or children, and generosity should come from one's own wealth.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: Fasting from food while cursing, backbiting or lying makes the fast pointless.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Tarawih's purpose is hearing the whole Quran; stay with the imam, sit if tired, and prefer the masjid to home.

quran.point: Whoever is ill or travelling makes up the days later: the basis for the concessions.
The ordered sequence of the major expiation: freeing a slave, two consecutive months, feeding sixty poor.
Fidyah of feeding a poor person for those who can only fast with hardship: the minor expiation.
Reaching extreme old age, the Quranic phrase he uses for the elderly exemption.
Elderly women past childbearing, cited for the fiqh of the elderly.

hadith.gist: Whoever eats or drinks forgetfully, it was Allah who fed him and gave him drink.
Whoever breaks a day of Ramadan without excuse cannot make it up even by fasting a lifetime.
There is blessing in suhoor; the Prophet's iftar and suhoor were a few dates, water and perhaps milk.
The Prophet's guidance is to delay suhoor and hasten iftar.
Break the fast on fresh dates, or dry dates if none, or water if none.
The dua of the fasting person when breaking the fast is not rejected.
Whoever does not abandon false speech and acting on it, Allah has no need for him to leave his food and drink.
The Prophet prayed thirteen rak'ahs at night.
hadith.source: Muslim (Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani), Bukhari (Ibn Abbas)

hadith.gist: Ibn Masud said he once intended something bad: to leave the Prophet in the prayer; and the man who left Muadh's long Isha was said to have become a hypocrite.
The soul is breathed into the fetus at 120 days, so zakat al-fitr is paid for it from then.

maxims: Whatever you deliberately take in that nourishes breaks the fast
The Quran preserved the language and the language preserved the Quran
Fasting is between you and Allah; you know yourself
The number of rak'ahs carries no weight; the Quran recited does
Pay the dues in their channels, then give from your own money

stories.point: Pupils in military uniform had to answer in classical Arabic; his teacher Omar al-Sabbagh punished colloquial answers, and his shaykh made them preach to trees and animals.

stories.who: A teacher who never attended school
stories.point: He knew the Alfiyyah of Ibn Malik and its commentaries by page, showing how the scholars honoured Arabic.
He was not given his Quran ijazah until he mastered prosody and composed classical poetry.

stories.who: Muslims in Germany and Scandinavia during summer Ramadans
stories.point: With near-endless days they should intend each fast and break it only when overwhelmed, making it up later.

stories.who: A man who fasted sixty consecutive days as expiation
stories.point: The hardship of the expiation brought him great benefit and success.

stories.who: Elderly diabetic women in emergency (his hospital work)
stories.point: They fasted against advice and came in at night with dangerously low or high sugar.

stories.who: Yearly offers of company zakat to the masjid
stories.point: He refuses zakat for the masjid even though the tent alone cost about $20,000.

contemporary: Decline of Arabic in Muslim lands; scholars in Morocco, Mauritania, Kuwait and Egypt raising it; Syria as the lost stronghold
People messaging the sheikh every Ramadan with the same basic questions (toothbrushing, eye drops)
Masjid finances: the roughly $20,000 tent; the masjid does not collect zakat or expiations
Islamic Relief and the share of zakat workers
Cost estimates: about $20 a meal, $1,200 for the major expiation, $600 fidyah for a month
Hunger across Muslim lands as an easy outlet for fidyah
Muslims in northern Europe fasting long summer days
Many separate Eid prayers in the city instead of one gathering
takeaways: Learn the general rule of what breaks the fast and stop re-asking the basics each year.
Take the concession when ill, pregnant, nursing or elderly; follow medical advice for diabetes and dialysis.
Make up missed days before next Ramadan and pay fidyah where required, directed to feeding the poor.
Give zakat and expiations to their prescribed recipients, then give generously from your own wealth.
Keep suhoor light, hasten iftar with dates, fast from sins, and pray tarawih until the imam finishes.

1:1.en: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful

1:2.en: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds

1:4.en: Master of the Day of Judgment

1:5.en: Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help

1:7.ar: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غَيۡرِ ٱلۡمَغۡضُوبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
1:7.en: The path of those whom Thou hast favoured; Not the (path) of those who earn Thine anger nor of those who go astray

2:153.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:153.en: O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast

2:154.ar: وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَن يُقۡتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَٰتُۢۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَآءࣱ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَشۡعُرُونَ
2:154.en: And call not those who are slain in the way of Allah "dead." Nay, they are living, only ye perceive not

2:155.ar: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:155.en: And surely We shall try you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and crops; but give glad tidings to the steadfast

2:156.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
2:156.en: Who say, when a misfortune striketh them: Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning

2:157.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَلَوَٰتࣱ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَرَحۡمَةࣱۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدُونَ
2:157.en: Such are they on whom are blessings from their Lord, and mercy. Such are the rightly guided

2:158.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:158.en: Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah. It is therefore no sin for him who is on pilgrimage to the House (of Allah) or visiteth it, to go around them (as the pagan custom is). And he who doeth good of his own accord, (for him) lo! Allah is Responsive, Aware

2:159.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا بَيَّنَّٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّٰعِنُونَ
2:159.en: Lo! Those who hide the proofs and the guidance which We revealed, after We had made it clear to mankind in the Scripture: such are accursed of Allah and accursed of those who have the power to curse

2:160.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَأَصۡلَحُواْ وَبَيَّنُواْ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَأَنَا ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:160.en: Except those who repent and amend and make manifest (the truth). These it is toward whom I relent. I am the Relenting, the Merciful

2:161.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارٌ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَعۡنَةُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
2:161.en: Lo! Those who disbelieve, and die while they are disbelievers; on them is the curse of Allah and of angels and of men combined

2:162.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ
2:162.en: They ever dwell therein. The doom will not be lightened for them, neither will they be reprieved

2:163.ar: وَإِلَٰهُكُمۡ إِلَٰهࣱ وَٰحِدࣱۖ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
2:163.en: Your Allah is One Allah; there is no Allah save Him, the Beneficent, the Merciful

2:164.ar: إِنَّ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ وَٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلَّتِي تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن مَّآءࣲ فَأَحۡيَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةࣲ وَتَصۡرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَٰحِ وَٱلسَّحَابِ ٱلۡمُسَخَّرِ بَيۡنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
2:164.en: Lo! In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of night and day, and the ships which run upon the sea with that which is of use to men, and the water which Allah sendeth down from the sky, thereby reviving the earth after its death, and dispersing all kinds of beasts therein, and (in) the ordinance of the winds, and the clouds obedient between heaven and earth: are signs (of Allah's Sovereignty) for people who have sense

2:165.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَندَادࣰ ا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبࣰّ ا لِّلَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
2:165.en: Yet of mankind are some who take unto themselves (objects of worship which they set as) rivals to Allah, loving them with a love like (that which is the due) of Allah (only) - those who believe are stauncher in their love for Allah - Oh, that those who do evil had but known, (on the day) when they behold the doom, that power belongeth wholly to Allah, and that Allah is severe in punishment

2:166.ar: إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَابُ
2:166.en: (On the day) when those who were followed disown those who followed (them), and they behold the doom, and all their aims collapse with them

2:167.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ لَوۡ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةࣰ فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُمۡ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُواْ مِنَّاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَمَا هُم بِخَٰرِجِينَ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
2:167.en: And those who were but followers will say: If a return were possible for us, we would disown them even as they have disowned us. Thus will Allah show them their own deeds as anguish for them, and they will not emerge from the Fire

2:168.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ كُلُواْ مِمَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ حَلَٰلࣰ ا طَيِّبࣰ ا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينٌ
2:168.en: O mankind! Eat of that which is lawful and wholesome in the earth, and follow not the footsteps of the devil. Lo! he is an open enemy for you

2:169.ar: إِنَّمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِٱلسُّوٓءِ وَٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَأَن تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:169.en: He enjoineth upon you only the evil and the foul, and that ye should tell concerning Allah that which ye know not

2:170.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
2:170.en: And when it is said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though their fathers were wholly unintelligent and had no guidance

2:171.ar: وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي يَنۡعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَآءࣰ وَنِدَآءࣰۚ صُمُّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡيࣱ فَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
2:171.en: The likeness of those who disbelieve (in relation to the messenger) is as the likeness of one who calleth unto that which heareth naught except a shout and cry. Deaf, dumb, blind, therefore they have no sense

2:172.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِلَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
2:172.en: O ye who believe! Eat of the good things wherewith We have provided you, and render thanks to Allah if it is (indeed) He Whom ye worship

2:173.ar: إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحۡمَ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِۦ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ غَيۡرَ بَاغࣲ وَلَا عَادࣲ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
2:173.en: He hath forbidden you only carrion, and blood, and swineflesh, and that which hath been immolated to (the name of) any other than Allah. But he who is driven by necessity, neither craving nor transgressing, it is no sin for him. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

2:174.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلًا أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
2:174.en: Lo! those who hide aught of the Scripture which Allah hath revealed and purchase a small gain therewith, they eat into their bellies nothing else than fire. Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He make them grow. Theirs will be a painful doom

2:175.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡعَذَابَ بِٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ فَمَآ أَصۡبَرَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ
2:175.en: Those are they who purchase error at the price of guidance, and torment at the price of pardon. How constant are they in their strife to reach the Fire

2:176.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ نَزَّلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَفِي شِقَاقِۭ بَعِيدࣲ‏
2:176.en: That is because Allah hath revealed the Scripture with the truth. Lo! those who find (a cause of) disagreement in the Scripture are in open schism

2:177.ar: ۞لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ
2:177.en: It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West; but righteous is he who believeth in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture and the prophets; and giveth wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk and to orphans and the needy and the wayfarer and to those who ask, and to set slaves free; and observeth proper worship and payeth the poor-due. And those who keep their treaty when they make one, and the patient in tribulation and adversity and time of stress. Such are they who are sincere. Such are the Allah-fearing

2:178.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِصَاصُ فِي ٱلۡقَتۡلَىۖ ٱلۡحُرُّ بِٱلۡحُرِّ وَٱلۡعَبۡدُ بِٱلۡعَبۡدِ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰ بِٱلۡأُنثَىٰۚ فَمَنۡ عُفِيَ لَهُۥ مِنۡ أَخِيهِ شَيۡءࣱ فَٱتِّبَاعُۢ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَأَدَآءٌ إِلَيۡهِ بِإِحۡسَٰنࣲۗ ذَٰلِكَ تَخۡفِيفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَةࣱۗ فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَهُۥ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ‏
2:178.en: O ye who believe! Retaliation is prescribed for you in the matter of the murdered; the freeman for the freeman, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. And for him who is forgiven somewhat by his (injured) brother, prosecution according to usage and payment unto him in kindness. This is an alleviation and a mercy from your Lord. He who transgresseth after this will have a painful doom

2:179.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡقِصَاصِ حَيَوٰةࣱ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:179.en: And there is life for you in retaliation, O men of understanding, that ye may ward off (evil)

2:180.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيۡرًا ٱلۡوَصِيَّةُ لِلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۖ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:180.en: It is prescribed for you, when death approacheth one of you, if he leave wealth, that he bequeath unto parents and near relatives in kindness. (This is) a duty for all those who ward off (evil)

2:181.ar: فَمَنۢ بَدَّلَهُۥ بَعۡدَ مَا سَمِعَهُۥ فَإِنَّمَآ إِثۡمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:181.en: And whoso changeth (the will) after he hath heard it - the sin thereof is only upon those who change it. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

2:182.ar: فَمَنۡ خَافَ مِن مُّوصࣲ جَنَفًا أَوۡ إِثۡمࣰ ا فَأَصۡلَحَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:182.en: But he who feareth from a testator some unjust or sinful clause, and maketh peace between the parties, (it shall be) no sin for him. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

2:183.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:183.en: O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil)

2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: (Fast) a certain number of days; and (for) him who is sick among you, or on a journey, (the same) number of other days; and for those who can afford it there is a ransom: the feeding of a man in need - but whoso doeth good of his own accord, it is better for him: and that ye fast is better for you if ye did but know

2:185.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدࣰ ى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
2:185.en: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful

2:186.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
2:186.en: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright

2:187.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسࣱ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسࣱ لَّهُنَّۗ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَعَفَا عَنكُمۡۖ فَٱلۡـَٰٔنَ بَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡخَيۡطُ ٱلۡأَبۡيَضُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡطِ ٱلۡأَسۡوَدِ مِنَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّواْ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَلَا تُبَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمۡ عَٰكِفُونَ فِي ٱلۡمَسَٰجِدِۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهَاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
2:187.en: It is made lawful for you to go in unto your wives on the night of the fast. They are raiment for you and ye are raiment for them. Allah is Aware that ye were deceiving yourselves in this respect and He hath turned in mercy toward you and relieved you. So hold intercourse with them and seek that which Allah hath ordained for you, and eat and drink until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn. Then strictly observe the fast till nightfall and touch them not, but be at your devotions in the mosques. These are the limits imposed by Allah, so approach them not. Thus Allah expoundeth His revelation to mankind that they may ward off (evil)

2:188.ar: وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَكُم بَيۡنَكُم بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتُدۡلُواْ بِهَآ إِلَى ٱلۡحُكَّامِ لِتَأۡكُلُواْ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:188.en: And eat not up your property among yourselves in vanity, nor seek by it to gain the hearing of the judges that ye may knowingly devour a portion of the property of others wrongfully

2:189.ar: ۞يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَهِلَّةِۖ قُلۡ هِيَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَلَيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرُّ بِأَن تَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبِهَاۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
2:189.en: They ask thee, (O Muhammad), of new moons, say: They are fixed seasons for mankind and for the pilgrimage. It is not righteousness that ye go to houses by the backs thereof (as do the idolaters at certain seasons), but the righteous man is he who wardeth off (evil). So go to houses by the gates thereof, and observe your duty to Allah, that ye may be successful

2:190.ar: وَقَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ وَلَا تَعۡتَدُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
2:190.en: Fight in the way of Allah against those who fight against you, but begin not hostilities. Lo! Allah loveth not aggressors

2:191.ar: وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ ثَقِفۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَأَخۡرِجُوهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ أَخۡرَجُوكُمۡۚ وَٱلۡفِتۡنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَتۡلِۚ وَلَا تُقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ عِندَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ حَتَّىٰ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِيهِۖ فَإِن قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡۗ كَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:191.en: And slay them wherever ye find them, and drive them out of the places whence they drove you out, for persecution is worse than slaughter. And fight not with them at the Inviolable Place of Worship until they first attack you there, but if they attack you (there) then slay them. Such is the reward of disbelievers

2:192.ar: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:192.en: But if they desist, then lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

2:193.ar: وَقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتۡنَةࣱ وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ لِلَّهِۖ فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:193.en: And fight them until persecution is no more, and religion is for Allah. But if they desist, then let there be no hostility except against wrong-doers

2:194.ar: ٱلشَّهۡرُ ٱلۡحَرَامُ بِٱلشَّهۡرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ وَٱلۡحُرُمَٰتُ قِصَاصࣱۚ فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَٱعۡتَدُواْ عَلَيۡهِ بِمِثۡلِ مَا ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:194.en: The forbidden month for the forbidden month, and forbidden things in retaliation. And one who attacketh you, attack him in like manner as he attacked you. Observe your duty to Allah, and know that Allah is with those who ward off (evil)

2:195.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تُلۡقُواْ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:195.en: Spend your wealth for the cause of Allah, and be not cast by your own hands to ruin; and do good. Lo! Allah loveth the beneficent

2:196.ar: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذࣰ ى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةࣱ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكࣲۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامࣲ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةࣱ كَامِلَةࣱۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
2:196.en: Perform the pilgrimage and the visit (to Makka) for Allah. And if ye are prevented, then send such gifts as can be obtained with ease, and shave not your heads until the gifts have reached their destination. And whoever among you is sick or hath an ailment of the head must pay a ransom of fasting or almsgiving or offering. And if ye are in safety, then whosoever contenteth himself with the visit for the pilgrimage (shall give) such gifts as can be had with ease. And whosoever cannot find (such gifts), then a fast of three days while on the pilgrimage, and of seven when ye have returned; that is, ten in all. That is for him whoso folk are not present at the Inviolable Place of Worship. Observe your duty to Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment

2:197.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرࣱ مَّعۡلُومَٰتࣱۚ فَمَن فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
2:197.en: The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months, and whoever is minded to perform the pilgrimage therein (let him remember that) there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage. And whatsoever good ye do Allah knoweth it. So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil. Therefore keep your duty unto Me, O men of understanding

2:198.ar: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتࣲ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
2:198.en: It is no sin for you that ye seek the bounty of your Lord (by trading). But, when ye press on in the multitude from 'Arafat, remember Allah by the sacred monument. Remember Him as He hath guided you, although before ye were of those astray

2:199.ar: ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:199.en: Then hasten onward from the place whence the multitude hasteneth onward, and ask forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

2:200.ar: فَإِذَا قَضَيۡتُم مَّنَٰسِكَكُمۡ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَذِكۡرِكُمۡ ءَابَآءَكُمۡ أَوۡ أَشَدَّ ذِكۡرࣰ اۗ فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَٰقࣲ‏
2:200.en: And when ye have completed your devotions, then remember Allah as ye remember your fathers or with a more lively remembrance. But of mankind is he who saith: "Our Lord! Give unto us in the world," and he hath no portion in the Hereafter

2:201.ar: وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةࣰ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ حَسَنَةࣰ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
2:201.en: And of them (also) is he who saith: "Our Lord! Give unto us in the world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and guard us from the doom of Fire

2:202.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ نَصِيبࣱ مِّمَّا كَسَبُواْۚ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
2:202.en: For them there is in store a goodly portion out of that which they have earned. Allah is swift at reckoning

2:203.ar: ۞وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيٓ أَيَّامࣲ مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۖ لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
2:203.en: Remember Allah through the appointed days. Then whoso hasteneth (his departure) by two days, it is no sin for him, and whoso delayeth, it is no sin for him; that is for him who wardeth off (evil). Be careful of your duty to Allah, and know that unto Him ye will be gathered

2:204.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعۡجِبُكَ قَوۡلُهُۥ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَيُشۡهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلۡخِصَامِ
2:204.en: And of mankind there is he whoso conversation on the life of this world pleaseth thee (Muhammad), and he calleth Allah to witness as to that which is in his heart; yet he is the most rigid of opponents

2:205.ar: وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُفۡسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡحَرۡثَ وَٱلنَّسۡلَۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَسَادَ
2:205.en: And when he turneth away (from thee) his effort in the land is to make mischief therein and to destroy the crops and the cattle; and Allah loveth not mischief

2:206.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ فَحَسۡبُهُۥ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَلَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
2:206.en: And when it is said unto him: Be careful of thy duty to Allah, pride taketh him to sin. Hell will settle his account, an evil resting-place

2:207.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشۡرِي نَفۡسَهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
2:207.en: And of mankind is he who would sell himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah; and Allah hath compassion on (His) bondmen

2:208.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱدۡخُلُواْ فِي ٱلسِّلۡمِ كَآفَّةࣰ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ مُّبِينࣱ‏
2:208.en: O ye who believe! Come, all of you, into submission (unto Him); and follow not the footsteps of the devil. Lo! he is an open enemy for you

2:209.ar: فَإِن زَلَلۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡكُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
2:209.en: And if ye slide back after the clear proofs have come unto you, then know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

2:210.ar: هَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ظُلَلࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡغَمَامِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
2:210.en: Wait they for naught else than that Allah should come unto them in the shadows of the clouds with the angels? Then the case would be already judged. All cases go back to Allah (for judgment)

2:211.ar: سَلۡ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ كَمۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ ءَايَةِۭ بَيِّنَةࣲۗ وَمَن يُبَدِّلۡ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
2:211.en: Ask of the Children of Israel how many a clear revelation We gave them! He who altereth the grace of Allah after it hath come unto him (for him), lo! Allah is severe in punishment

2:212.ar: زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَيَسۡخَرُونَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۘ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابࣲ‏
2:212.en: Beautified is the life of the world for those who disbelieve; they make a jest of the believers. But those who keep their duty to Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. Allah giveth without stint to whom He will

2:213.ar: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۚ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ
2:213.en: Mankind were one community, and Allah sent (unto them) prophets as bearers of good tidings and as warners, and revealed therewith the Scripture with the truth that it might judge between mankind concerning that wherein they differed. And only those unto whom (the Scripture) was given differed concerning it, after clear proofs had come unto them, through hatred one of another. And Allah by His Will guided those who believe unto the truth of that concerning which they differed. Allah guideth whom He will unto a straight path

2:246.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَإِ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مُوسَىٰٓ إِذۡ قَالُواْ لِنَبِيࣲّ لَّهُمُ ٱبۡعَثۡ لَنَا مَلِكࣰ ا نُّقَٰتِلۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ قَالَ هَلۡ عَسَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ أَلَّا تُقَٰتِلُواْۖ قَالُواْ وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نُقَٰتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَدۡ أُخۡرِجۡنَا مِن دِيَٰرِنَا وَأَبۡنَآئِنَاۖ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ تَوَلَّوۡاْ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:246.en: Bethink thee of the leaders of the Children of Israel after Moses, how they said unto a prophet whom they had: Set up for us a king and we will fight in Allah's way. He said: Would ye then refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you? They said: Why should we not fight in Allah's way when we have been driven from our dwellings with our children? Yet, when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, all save a few of them. Allah is aware of evil-doers

2:247.ar: وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ نَبِيُّهُمۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ بَعَثَ لَكُمۡ طَالُوتَ مَلِكࣰ اۚ قَالُوٓاْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ عَلَيۡنَا وَنَحۡنُ أَحَقُّ بِٱلۡمُلۡكِ مِنۡهُ وَلَمۡ يُؤۡتَ سَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَالِۚ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصۡطَفَىٰهُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَزَادَهُۥ بَسۡطَةࣰ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ وَٱلۡجِسۡمِۖ وَٱللَّهُ يُؤۡتِي مُلۡكَهُۥ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
2:247.en: Their Prophet said unto them: Lo! Allah hath raised up Saul to be a king for you. They said: How can he have kingdom over us when we are more deserving of the kingdom than he is, since he hath not been given wealth enough? He said: Lo! Allah hath chosen him above you, and hath increased him abundantly in wisdom and stature. Allah bestoweth His Sovereignty on whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing

2:248.ar: وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ نَبِيُّهُمۡ إِنَّ ءَايَةَ مُلۡكِهِۦٓ أَن يَأۡتِيَكُمُ ٱلتَّابُوتُ فِيهِ سَكِينَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَبَقِيَّةࣱ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ءَالُ مُوسَىٰ وَءَالُ هَٰرُونَ تَحۡمِلُهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
2:248.en: And their Prophet said unto them: Lo! the token of his kingdom is that there shall come unto you the ark wherein is peace of reassurance from your Lord, and a remnant of that which the house of Moses and the house of Aaron left behind, the angels bearing it. Lo! herein shall be a token for you if (in truth) ye are believers

2:249.ar: فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبۡتَلِيكُم بِنَهَرࣲ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنۡهُ فَلَيۡسَ مِنِّي وَمَن لَّمۡ يَطۡعَمۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغۡتَرَفَ غُرۡفَةَۢ بِيَدِهِۦۚ فَشَرِبُواْ مِنۡهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡۚ فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُۥ هُوَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ قَالُواْ لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ ٱللَّهِ كَم مِّن فِئَةࣲ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةࣰ كَثِيرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:249.en: And when Saul set out with the army, he said: Lo! Allah will try you by (the ordeal of) a river. Whosoever therefore drinketh thereof he is not of me, and whosoever tasteth it not he is of me, save him who taketh (thereof) in the hollow of his hand. But they drank thereof, all save a few of them. And after he had crossed (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts. But those who knew that they would meet Allah exclaimed: How many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave! Allah is with the steadfast

2:250.ar: وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرࣰ ا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:250.en: And when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts they said: Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance, make our foothold sure, and give us help against the disbelieving folk

2:251.ar: فَهَزَمُوهُم بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَقَتَلَ دَاوُۥدُ جَالُوتَ وَءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَعَلَّمَهُۥ مِمَّا يَشَآءُۗ وَلَوۡلَا دَفۡعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضࣲ لَّفَسَدَتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
2:251.en: So they routed them by Allah's leave and David slew Goliath; and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom, and taught him of that which He willeth. And if Allah had not repelled some men by others the earth would have been corrupted. But Allah is a Lord of Kindness to (His) creatures

2:252.ar: تِلۡكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱللَّهِ نَتۡلُوهَا عَلَيۡكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلِينَ
2:252.en: These are the portents of Allah which We recite unto thee (Muhammad) with truth, and lo! thou art of the number of (Our) messengers

2:253.ar: ۞تِلۡكَ ٱلرُّسُلُ فَضَّلۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲۘ مِّنۡهُم مَّن كَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُۖ وَرَفَعَ بَعۡضَهُمۡ دَرَجَٰتࣲۚ وَءَاتَيۡنَا عِيسَى ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَأَيَّدۡنَٰهُ بِرُوحِ ٱلۡقُدُسِۗ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا ٱقۡتَتَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ وَلَٰكِنِ ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فَمِنۡهُم مَّنۡ ءَامَنَ وَمِنۡهُم مَّن كَفَرَۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا ٱقۡتَتَلُواْ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفۡعَلُ مَا يُرِيدُ
2:253.en: Of those messengers, some of whom We have caused to excel others, and of whom there are some unto whom Allah spake, while some of them He exalted (above others) in degree; and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty) and We supported him with the holy Spirit. And if Allah had so wiled it, those who followed after them would not have fought one with another after the clear proofs had come unto them. But they differed, some of them believing and some disbelieving. And if Allah had so willed it, they would not have fought one with another; but Allah doeth what He will

2:254.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ يَوۡمࣱ لَّا بَيۡعࣱ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةࣱ وَلَا شَفَٰعَةࣱۗ وَٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
2:254.en: O ye who believe! spend of that wherewith We have provided you ere a day come when there will be no trafficking, nor friendship, nor intercession. The disbelievers, they are the wrong-doers

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. His throne includeth the heavens and the earth, and He is never weary of preserving them. He is the Sublime, the Tremendous

2:256.ar: لَآ إِكۡرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشۡدُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيِّۚ فَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:256.en: There is no compulsion in religion. The right direction is henceforth distinct from error. And he who rejecteth false deities and believeth in Allah hath grasped a firm handhold which will never break. Allah is Hearer, Knower

2:257.ar: ٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُخۡرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآؤُهُمُ ٱلطَّٰغُوتُ يُخۡرِجُونَهُم مِّنَ ٱلنُّورِ إِلَى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:257.en: Allah is the Protecting Guardian of those who believe. He bringeth them out of darkness into light. As for those who disbelieve, their patrons are false deities. They bring them out of light into darkness. Such are rightful owners of the Fire. They will abide therein

2:258.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ فِي رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنۡ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ إِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّيَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحۡيِۦ وَأُمِيتُۖ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡتِي بِٱلشَّمۡسِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ فَأۡتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:258.en: Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom; how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death, he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said: Lo! Allah causeth the sun to rise in the East, so do thou cause it to come up from the West. Thus was the disbeliever abashed. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

2:259.ar: أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةࣲ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحۡيِۦ هَٰذِهِ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۖ فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِاْئَةَ عَامࣲ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُۥۖ قَالَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتَۖ قَالَ لَبِثۡتُ يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲۖ قَالَ بَل لَّبِثۡتَ مِاْئَةَ عَامࣲ فَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمۡ يَتَسَنَّهۡۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجۡعَلَكَ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعِظَامِ كَيۡفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكۡسُوهَا لَحۡمࣰ اۚ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥ قَالَ أَعۡلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:259.en: Or (bethink thee of) the like of him who, passing by a township which had fallen into utter ruin, exclaimed: How shall Allah give this township life after its death? And Allah made him die a hundred years, then brought him back to life. He said: How long hast thou tarried? (The man) said: I have tarried a day or part of a day. (He) said: Nay, but thou hast tarried for a hundred years. Just look at thy food and drink which have not rotted! Look at thine ass! And, that We may make thee a token unto mankind, look at the bones, how We adjust them and then cover them with flesh! And when (the matter) became clear unto him, he said: I know now that Allah is Able to do all things

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

2:85.ar: ثُمَّ أَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تَقۡتُلُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَتُخۡرِجُونَ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ تَظَٰهَرُونَ عَلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَإِن يَأۡتُوكُمۡ أُسَٰرَىٰ تُفَٰدُوهُمۡ وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِخۡرَاجُهُمۡۚ أَفَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِبَعۡضِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَتَكۡفُرُونَ بِبَعۡضࣲۚ فَمَا جَزَآءُ مَن يَفۡعَلُ ذَٰلِكَ مِنكُمۡ إِلَّا خِزۡيࣱ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰٓ أَشَدِّ ٱلۡعَذَابِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
2:85.en: Yet ye it is who slay each other and drive out a party of your people from their homes, supporting one another against them by sin and transgression? - and if they came to you as captives ye would ransom them, whereas their expulsion was itself unlawful for you - Believe ye in part of the Scripture and disbelieve ye in part thereof? And what is the reward of those who do so save ignominy in the life of the world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be consigned to the most grievous doom. For Allah is not unaware of what ye do

58:18.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيَحۡلِفُونَ لَهُۥ كَمَا يَحۡلِفُونَ لَكُمۡ وَيَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءٍۚ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
58:18.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together, then will they swear unto Him as they (now) swear unto you, and they will fancy that they have some standing. Lo! is it not they who are the liars
